44770215.article_content:
Martin Couney holds up Beth Allen, a premature baby who was on view at the Coney Island attraction.
Beth Allen
Nurses in starched white uniforms and doctors in medical coats tended to babies in glass and steel incubators. The infants had been born many weeks premature and well below a healthy birth weight. Stores didn’t make clothes small enough to fit their tiny, skeletal frames so the nurses dressed them in dolls’ clothes and knitted bonnets.
A sign above the entrance read “Living Babies in Incubators” in letters so large they could be read from the other end of the Chicago World’s Fair grounds, which took place over 18 months in 1933 and 1934. The infant incubator exhibit was built at a cost of $75,000 (worth $1.4 million today) and was painted in a patriotic red, white and blue.
The men in charge were leading Chicago pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess and Martin Couney, who was known across America as “the incubator doctor.” Couney was a lugubrious man in his 60s, with thinning gray hair, a mustache and a stoop, something he jokingly attributed to a lifetime of bending over babies. Couney and Hess employed a team of six nurses and two wet nurses.
Martin Couney had run infant incubator exhibits, in which premature babies were displayed to the public, for more than three decades, most famously at Coney Island in New York City. He had long been regarded by desperate parents as a savior, one who offered medical help to babies written off as “weaklings” by mainstream medicine.
But for Hess, who was accustomed to carrying out his work in a more conventional hospital setting, this was a career first.
Miracle at Coney Island: How a Sideshow Doctor Saved Thousands of Babies and Transformed American Medicine (Kindle Single)
More about this product
The exhibit was a hit with the Chicago public who paid 25 cents and flocked by the hundreds of thousands to see the babies.
To celebrate the success of their facility, Couney organized a “Homecoming” celebration on July 25, 1934, for babies who had “graduated” from the incubators at the Chicago’s World’s Fair the previous summer. Of the 58 babies Couney and Hess had cared for in 1933, 41 returned with their mothers for the reunion. The event was broadcast live on local radio and across the fairgrounds.
On the radio program, Couney’s exhibit was portrayed by the announcer not as a frivolous sideshow spectacle, but as an invaluable medical facility:
The Incubator station for premature babies…is not primarily a place of exhibiting tiny infants. Instead, it is actually a lifesaving station, where prematurely born babies are brought from leading hospitals all over the city, for the care and attention that are afforded. The place is spick and span, with doctors and graduate nurses in constant attendance...
Because of the sideshow setting in which he operated, Couney’s career had always been controversial. Many in the medical professional viewed the “incubator doctor” with suspicion, others with outright hostility. The New York Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children had repeatedly accused Couney of exploiting the babies and endangering their lives by putting them on show.
None of the complaints was sustained, and by the 1930s, Couney was finally being taken seriously as a medical pioneer. Couney’s professional collaboration with Hess marked a key stage in his habilitation.
But while doing research for my radio documentary
Life Under Glass
, which is being broadcast on NPR stations around the country this August, and my book,
Miracle at Coney Island
, I made an incredible discovery about a man who has a claim to have changed the course of American neonatal medicine.
Couney never actually qualified as a medical doctor.
Throughout his career, Couney said he had studied medicine in Leipzig and Berlin. However, I could find no evidence of Couney (or Cohn/Cohen as he was known then) having studied medicine at a university in either city. To become a physician in Germany, one was required to write a thesis. The U.S. National Library of Medicine has copies of the German records: the librarians could not locate a thesis written by Couney.
Couney was deliberately evasive about his date and place of birth. I have discovered that he immigrated to the US in 1888 at 19 years old. But someone of that age would not be old enough to have studied at university in Leipzig and Berlin before going on to do graduate work in Paris at the knee of Pierre Budin, the father of European neonatal medicine, as Couney claimed to have done in numerous press interviews.
In the 1910 U.S. census, Couney listed his career as, “surgical instruments.” Though Couney claimed to be the inventor of an incubator, I have been unable to find any evidence that he registered an incubator patent in the U.S. More likely Couney was a technician. Yet by 1930 he was describing himself in the census as a “physician.”

data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 文章宣布2025年8月5日是cURL项目发布以来的第10,000天，称为"c10kday"。为了庆祝这一时刻，项目团队邀请用户分享与cURL相关的故事，包括首次使用cURL的经历、cURL如何帮助解决问题的实例以及它对个人工作或生活的意义。这些故事将在cURL的GitHub讨论区收集和分享，虽然团队在持续开发新功能和修复漏洞，但这个日子依然是与社区互动并回顾美好记忆的契机。最后，文章感谢用户对cURL的支持。

44797050.article_content:
From
March 20, 1998
when the first curl release was published, to this day
August 5, 2025
is exactly 10,000 days. We call it the curl-10000-day. Or just
c10kday
. c ten K day.
We want to celebrate this occasion by collecting and sharing stories. Your stories about curl. Your favorite memories. When you used curl for the first time. When curl saved your situation. When curl rescued your lost puppy. What curl has meant or perhaps still means to you, your work, your business, or your life. We want to favor and prioritize the good, the fun, the nostalgic and the emotional stories but it is of course up to your discretion.
We have created this thread in curl’s GitHub Discussion section for this purpose, so please go there and submit your story or read what others have shared.
https://github.com/curl/curl/discussions/17930
In the curl factory this day is nothing special. We keep hammering out new features and bugfixes – just like we always do.
Thanks for flying curl.

Apache ECharts 6.0 发布了12项重大升级，旨在提升数据可视化的专业性和灵活性。主要改进围绕三个核心维度：

1. **更专业的视觉表现**：
   - 全新默认主题，现代设计语言。
   - 动态主题切换，无需重新初始化图表。
   - 支持暗黑模式，自动适配系统主题。

2. **扩展数据表达边界**：
   - 新增和弦图、蜂群图、散点抖动、断轴等新图表和功能，处理复杂数据场景。
   - 增强股票交易图表，提升标签能力和开箱即用的图表类型。

3. **释放组合自由**：
   - 新的矩阵坐标系，支持像表格一样组合图表和组件。
   - 增强的自定义系列，支持npm发布和动态注册。
   - 新增小提琴图、轮廓图等自定义图表。
   - 优化轴标签布局，防止重叠。

这些升级使ECharts 6.0在数据可视化方面更加强大、可靠和灵活，帮助开发者创造出更具创意的视觉作品。

主要讨论点：ECharts库的优缺点及适用场景

不同观点：
• **支持ECharts，强调其功能丰富和易用性**：
  - ECharts被认为是功能齐全、易于上手的图表库，适用于复杂的数据密集型图表（ggregoire, kylecordes）。
  - 支持React，并且在多Y轴等复杂需求上表现良好（ggregoire）。
  - 与商业库相比，ECharts在功能和灵活性上占优，尤其在实时数据库可视化中表现出色（RyanHamilton）。
  - 支持动画、易于集成和使用，尤其是在Vue中表现良好（porridgeraisin）。

• **指出ECharts的不足和扩展困难**：
  - 扩展功能较为困难，例如实现甘特图需要深入源码（kakadu）。
  - 图表数据结构不统一，不同图表类型需要不同数据结构，文档不够完善（rorylaitila）。
  - 翻译和国际化支持不佳（kakadu）。

• **比较与其他图表库**：
  - 在与uPlot、Highcharts、Chart.js、C3.js、Ag-Grid等库比较中，ECharts因其动画支持、易用性和可靠性胜出（porridgeraisin）。
  - 有用户考虑从Highcharts切换到ECharts（tnolet）。

• **特定功能需求**：
  - 有用户询问ECharts是否支持交互式3D图表（billfruit）。
  - 用户关注ECharts在实时图表和实时数据处理方面的应用（nirav72）。
  - 用户寻找Sankey图表的支持（hbarka）。

补充讨论：
• **向后兼容性和迁移成本**：
  - 用户对ECharts的向后兼容性表示赞赏，尤其是从其他库迁移时工作量较小（homebrewer）。
  
• **性能和优化**：
  - 有用户提到ECharts在处理大数据量和频繁用户交互时的性能表现良好，且在处理缺失数据时无需额外处理（porridgeraisin）。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于ECharts的功能扩展难度和文档不完善的问题，部分用户在实现特定图表类型时遇到困难（kakadu, rorylaitila）。

Apache ECharts 6 New Features
Twelve years ago, ECharts was first released on GitHub, planting the seed for an open-source journey.
From a simple charting tool to a visualization powerhouse supporting millions of developers; from a single front-end charting library to a comprehensive technology system covering mobile, large screens, and server-side rendering—over these 12 years, we've witnessed ECharts' continuous technical breakthroughs and have been delighted to see developers worldwide create countless stunning data stories with ECharts.
Now, Apache ECharts 6.0 is officially released, bringing 12 major upgrades to take your data visualization to the next level.
Feature Overview
Twelve years of accumulation, all for more ultimate visual expression. The core strength of Apache ECharts has always come from a deep understanding of developers' real challenges. When defining the direction for 6.0, the question was clear:
How can we make complex data presentation both powerful and elegant?
This drove us to evolve deeply around three core dimensions:
More professional visual presentation
: From a meticulously crafted default theme to intelligent dark mode switching, ensuring charts have a professional look and seamlessly integrate into modern applications.
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
: New chart types and features to handle complex scenarios and enable intuitive expression of deep data.
Unleashing freedom of composition
: From the revolutionary matrix coordinate system to reusable custom series and optimized axis labels—empowering developers to freely compose and turn creativity into unconstrained visual works.
We have made 12 upgrades across these three core dimensions. These are not just simple feature additions, but a solid foundation for building the next generation of data-driven applications. They all point to one goal:
to make ECharts powerful, reliable, and stable in the background, leaving the stage and spotlight for your creative expression.
Below, we introduce these twelve upgrades in detail:
More professional visual presentation
1. Brand New Default Theme
: Modern design language for professional data expression
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
: Seamless runtime theme switching for multi-theme scenarios
3. Dark Mode Support
: Automatically adapts to system dark/light mode for better UX
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
4. New Chord Chart
: Visualize complex relationships and distributions
5. New Beeswarm Chart
: Smartly expand overlapping data points into a honeycomb layout
6. New Scatter Jittering
: Add jitter to scatter plots for better readability of dense data
7. New Broken Axis
: Easily present data with large magnitude differences
8. Enhanced Stock Trading Charts
: Improved label capabilities and more out-of-the-box trading charts
Unleashing freedom of composition
9. New Matrix Coordinate System
: Freely combine chart types and components like a table
10. Enhanced Custom Series
: Support npm publishing and dynamic registration for code reuse
11. New Custom Charts
: Violin, contour, stage, bar range, and line range charts
12. Axis Label Optimization
: Smarter default axis label layout to prevent overflow and overlap
With these upgrades, Apache ECharts 6.0 helps users create more charts more flexibly and conveniently, truly achieving "unlimited possibilities in charting"!
Feature Details
1. Brand New Default Theme
During the development of ECharts 6.0, we analyzed real user scenarios and found that over 70% of developers use the default theme. This made us realize: an excellent default theme should not only be aesthetically pleasing but also meet the general needs of various business scenarios.
The new theme system uses design tokens to reconstruct colors, spacing, and other design elements,
making different chart types and components more harmonious and consistent
.
Although the 6.0 theme has significant changes from 5.x, we provide a
v5.js
theme file for developers who want to use new features but keep the old style for quick migration.
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
In previous versions, changing a chart's theme required disposing of the chart instance and re-initializing, which could negatively impact user experience due to repeated animations. In the new version, we implemented
dynamic theme switching
(see documentation), significantly improving the user experience.
3. Dark Mode Support
With dynamic theme registration and switching, a typical scenario is
listening to the system's dark mode and dynamically adjusting the chart's theme
.
This is crucial for business scenarios supporting dark mode, ensuring the application interface matches the system theme and greatly enhancing user experience.

data.title: The Disappearance of Saturday Morning (2003)
data.author: KoftaBob
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：星期六早晨卡通消失的原因和影响

不同观点：
• [simmonmt] 认为《儿童电视法案》（Children's Television Act）及其引入的教育与信息性（E/I）节目可能是导致星期六早晨卡通消失的重要因素，并指出文章遗漏了这一点。他提供了维基百科链接作为参考，强调E/I节目的影响。
• [hackpit] 从个人经历出发，认为限制看电视的时间（如只能在特定时间看电视）也是造成这种文化现象消失的原因之一。他怀念如《Wile E. Coyote》这样的经典卡通，并提到过去孩子们只能在特定时间看电视，随后被要求出去玩耍。
• [JKCalhoun] 描述了自己通过技术手段（Raspberry Pi和自编程序）重建类似童年电视节目表的体验。他强调了现代技术如何帮助重现过去的观看体验，同时指出没有广告和随机填充短片的体验。他还提到自己程序的不足之处以及未来的改进计划。
• [1970-01-01] 认为ATSC 3.0技术和流媒体的普及将很快使非直播广播像AM广播一样消失，预示着传统广播电视的终结。
• [georgeburdell] 对比了2000年代和70、80年代的卡通质量，指出70、80年代也有大量低质量的Hanna-Barbera卡通，质疑文章对卡通质量下降的批评。
• [neuroelectron] 提出担忧，认为如果孩子们不能外出，共享体验（如看卡通）可能成为他们社交的重要途径，而这并不是理想的情况。
• [deadbabe] 从心理时间感的角度分析，认为星期六早晨卡通对孩子们的意义在于它标志着经过漫长学校周后的放松和自由时光，这种期待感增加了卡通的特殊性。

补充讨论：
• [teiferer] 认为文章标题"Disappearance of Saturday Morning"过于宽泛，建议改为更具体的"Disappearance of Saturday Morning Kids Cartoons on TV"，以更准确地反映文章内容和特定受众。
• [throawaywpg] 简单直接地指出，过去的星期六早晨卡通大多只是玩具广告的延伸，质量未必高。

争议焦点：
• 对于导致星期六早晨卡通消失的主要原因，存在不同看法。simmonmt强调法律和E/I节目的影响，而hackpit则关注个人经历和家庭规定的作用。
• 卡通质量的历史对比，georgeburdell质疑文章对2000年代卡通质量下降的批评，认为70、80年代也有大量低质量卡通。

data.title: Weather satellites detect 515-mile-long lightning flash
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 2017年，一场雷暴产生了一道惊人的闪电，长度达515英里（829公里），创下世界纪录。这一巨型闪电（megaflash）从德克萨斯州延伸至密苏里州，打破了2020年创下的477英里（768公里）的纪录。巨型闪电定义为长度至少达到62英里（100公里）的闪电，而普通闪电通常不到10英里（16公里）。研究团队利用GOES-16卫星的数据确认了这一长度。这类巨型闪电非常罕见，通常需要持续约14小时的雷暴才可能产生。随着闪电测绘技术的进步，未来可能会发现更多此类极端现象。研究结果发表在《美国气象学会公报》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕闪电和距离测量的相关讨论，包括闪电的性质、范围记录以及数据处理问题。

不同观点：
• [hansvm] 认为当前的技术和现象（如电子邮件和闪电）在约500英里的范围内停滞不前，暗示技术或自然现象存在某种限制。链接的文章也讨论了类似的问题。
• [kitd] 关注闪电的机制，特别是图示中正负分支的闪光，猜测是多个放电引发的连锁反应，并询问其他人是否了解其工作原理。
• [Sebb767] 通过将515英里转换为公里和美式足球场的长度来提供一个直观的度量，帮助读者理解距离的实际概念。

补充讨论：
• [ourmandave] 提到木星上出现的宽于地球的雷暴和绿色闪电，引用了相关文章，增加了讨论的趣味性，并将话题扩展到天文和外太空现象。
• [theandrewbailey] 对2017年的闪电打破2020年的记录表示困惑，质疑为何早期事件能超越后期事件，并指出文章中没有解释为何之前的数据未被发现，暗示数据处理可能存在问题。
• [morjom] 关注闪电的具体类型，询问其他人是否知道该闪电是云内闪还是云对地闪，显示出对闪电分类的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• [theandrewbailey] 提出的数据处理问题，质疑为何2017年的闪电记录在2020年之后才被发现，并认为文章没有充分解释这一现象，暗示数据管理和历史记录中可能存在漏洞或不一致。

44768778.article_content:
Some areas are more prone to lightning storms than others.
(Image credit: John finney photography/Getty Images)
It's 2017, and a thunderstorm shoots off a lightning bolt. What's so special about that, you ask? Well, the bolt is an astonishing 515 miles (829 kilometers) long.
Using archival satellite data, researchers just officially confirmed the length of this enormous bolt of lightning that stretched from Texas to Missouri. It sets a new world record, besting the previous title holder — a
477-mile (768-km) bolt from 2020
— by 38 miles (61 km).
"​​We call it megaflash lightning and we're just now figuring out the mechanics of how and why it occurs," Randy Cerveny, an Arizona State University professor who contributed to the study, said in a
statement
.
You may like
When lightning bolts collide, do they unleash powerful gamma-ray flashes?
Watch the sun unleash 600,000-mile-long eruption in fiery outburst (video)
Lightning from above | Space photo of the day for May 23, 2025
Megaflash lightning is defined as a lightning bolt that reaches at least 62 miles (100 km) in length. By comparison, the average lightning bolt measures less than 10 miles (16 km) in length. (Fun fact, most lightning is just an inch or so wide.)
To determine this length of the record-holding megaflash, the team reviewed data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's
GOES-16 satellite
, which is equipped with a lightning mapper that observes about one million bolts per day. Their analysis determined the true length of the bolt: a whopping 515 miles.
So, how exactly does one measure a megaflash? Previously, researchers used ground-based radio networks to track lightning bolts. However, satellites with lightning mappers are updating the process.
GOES-16 satellite image recording a record-setting 515-mile ligtning megaflash during a storm in October 2017. Red circles mark positively charged branches of the lightning, and blue circles mark negatively charged branches.
(Image credit: NOAA)
"Adding continuous measurements from
geostationary orbit
was a major advance," Michael Peterson of Georgia Tech Research Institute, who served as lead author of a paper on the study, said in the statement. "We are now at a point where most of the global megaflash hotspots are covered by a geostationary satellite, and data processing techniques have improved to properly represent flashes in the vast quantity of observational data at all scales."

Megaflashes like these are quite rare — less than one percent of thunderstorms produce them. Typically speaking, the thunderstorms that indeed manage to produce them must be churning for 14 hours or more, covering an area at least the size of the state of New Jersey, per Peterson's research.

Those conditions aren't altogether
that
rare, to be fair. And, as our lightning-mapping satellites collect new data, we'll probably start noticing even more megaflashes. "It is likely that even greater extremes still exist, and that we will be able to observe them as additional high-quality lightning measurements accumulate over time," said Cerveny,
A paper on the research was published in the
Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
.

44768778.article_summary: 2017年，一场雷暴产生了一道惊人的闪电，长度达515英里（829公里），创下世界纪录。这一巨型闪电（megaflash）从德克萨斯州延伸至密苏里州，打破了2020年创下的477英里（768公里）的纪录。巨型闪电定义为长度至少达到62英里（100公里）的闪电，而普通闪电通常不到10英里（16公里）。研究团队利用GOES-16卫星的数据确认了这一长度。这类巨型闪电非常罕见，通常需要持续约14小时的雷暴才可能产生。随着闪电测绘技术的进步，未来可能会发现更多此类极端现象。研究结果发表在《美国气象学会公报》上。

data.title: More than two hard disks in DOS
data.author: yuhong
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了Microsoft OS/2 1.21磁盘驱动程序的异常行为，并追溯到Compaq的EXTDISK.SYS驱动程序。研究发现，DOS 5.0之前的版本不支持超过两个由BIOS暴露的硬盘，若硬盘过多，系统可能会在启动时挂起。这一问题源于早期PC硬件限制，当时大多数电脑由于物理空间和电源限制，无法安装超过两个全高5¼英寸硬盘。

Compaq和Adaptec在1988年左右分别推出了支持更多硬盘的解决方案。Compaq通过不通过BIOS暴露额外硬盘，而是通过EXTDISK.SYS驱动让DOS用户访问。Adaptec则通过其AHA-154x SCSI卡和ASPI驱动解决该问题。

DOS 5.0之前版本的bug导致系统无法处理超过两个硬盘，具体表现为MS-DOS内核在计算文件系统参数时进入无限循环。该问题在DOS 2.0到4.0版本中普遍存在，直到DOS 5.0才得以解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：早期PC硬件限制导致硬盘数量受限的问题

不同观点：
• [blueflow] 认为早期主板通常只有一个IDE/平行ATA端口，每个端口只能支持两个可寻址驱动器（主驱动和从驱动）。如果有第二个ATA端口，则最多只能支持四个驱动器。这是硬件限制导致的，并解释了启动时屏幕上显示的"primary master"文本的来源。

• [mikeytown2] 指出，带有IDE端口的声卡用于连接CD-ROM驱动器在当时也是很常见的配置。

• [philipstorry] 表示对早期硬件配置的怀念，并提到自己在Windows 7和SATA时代之前很少使用超过2个固定磁盘。他进一步解释了IDE和SATA之前的硬盘配置情况，通常只有两个控制器，每个控制器支持两个设备。他还提到如果需要更多磁盘，可以使用SCSI，但SCSI支持在PC上的表现不佳，可能让人选择UNIX工作站。

补充讨论：
• [tempodox] 以幽默的方式质疑，如果640KB的内存已经足够，那么要那么多硬盘干什么，暗示早期PC的硬件需求和现代需求的不同。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于早期PC硬件的限制是否真的导致了一些技术问题未被发现。具体来说，是否因为早期硬件配置的限制（如硬盘数量）使得某些软件问题未被及时发现和解决。

• 另一个潜在的争议点是SCSI在早期PC中的表现问题，有人认为SCSI提供了更多磁盘支持但表现不佳，可能影响用户选择更专业的计算平台如UNIX工作站。

44796698.article_content:
Investigating the rather odd behavior of the
Microsoft OS/2 1.21 disk driver
led me to
Compaq and their EXTDISK.SYS driver
. While experimenting with various setups, I realized that DOS versions older than 5.0 do not support more than two hard disks exposed by the system’s BIOS, and will in fact quite likely hang early during boot-up if there are “too many” hard disks.
This seems to have been one of the many things that “everyone knew” back in the day, similar to the fact that DOS versions older than 3.3 may
hang while booting
from disks with significantly more than 17 sectors per track.
As was the case with the “too many sectors per track” problem, the issue with “too many hard disks” was missed for years simply because no one had a PC with more than two hard disks. This was a technical rather than architectural limitation. While the IBM PC/XT and PC/AT BIOS implementations were limited to two hard disks, the INT 13h interface as such was not.
In the days of full-height 5¼” drives, it simply was not feasible to install more than two hard disks into a PC, especially when a 5¼” floppy drive was also required. Even the big IBM PS/2 Model 80 (1987) with a tower case could only house two full-height 5¼” drives. There might also be trouble with the power supply, as the PC hard disks of the time were not designed for staggered spin-up and a standard AT power supply might have trouble spinning up four drives at the same time.
Sure, there were half-height hard disks, but who wanted four drives in the first place? People who needed to maximize the storage capacity… and the most obvious way to do that was buying a large capacity drive, which in the 1980s was inevitably a full-height 5¼” monster. Like my
1988-model 650 MB ESDI drive
, for example.
Yes, there were solutions like the NetWare DCB which supported many drives, but those were only usable by NetWare and did not expose the drives via INT 13h.
Two things happened circa 1988. One was Compaq releasing the Deskpro 386/25 with an expansion unit option, a system which supported up to four hard AT-style disks (that is, the expansion unit housed up to two ESDI drives accessible via the PC/AT hard disk style programming interface, which may be called WD1003 or WD1010 or several other things). The other development was Adaptec releasing the AHA-1540/1542 SCSI HBA, and there were perhaps other SCSI vendors as well.
Compaq supported up to four hard disks, Adaptec in theory up to seven. In any case, it is apparent that both companies ran into the same problem with DOS, and solved it in a very similar manner.
Compaq simply did not expose the drives in the expansion unit through the BIOS at all. DOS users needed the EXTDISK.SYS driver, and users of other operating systems (such as OS/2 or NetWare) needed a custom driver.
Adaptec was in a more complicated situation. The AHA-154x was an add-on card which could be installed in a PC/AT compatible machine (the AHA-154x did not work in older systems because it was a bus-mastering adapter) that already had one or two AT style drives. The AHA-154x BIOS keeps the total hard disk maximum to two. In practice that means that if there are two SCSI hard disks attached to an AHA-154x (which also includes AHA-154xA and AHA-154xB, but not necessarily newer models), the Adaptec BIOS may add zero, one, or two drives to the system, depending on how many hard disks there are already installed. In any case, the total won’t be greater than two.
For DOS users, Adaptec offered a combination of ASPI4DOS.SYS (ASPI driver for the AHA-154x) plus ASPIDISK.SYS (DOS hard disk device driver). Adaptec’s ASPIDISK.SYS was functionally very similar to Compaq’s EXTDISK.SYS and allowed DOS users (especially users of DOS 4.x and older) to utilize more than two hard disks.
DOS Bug
The bug is quite visible in the MS-DOS 4.0 source code. In MSINIT.ASM (IO.SYS/IBMBIO.COM module), DOS
calls INT 13h/08h
and stores the number of disks in the HNUM variable. No attempt is made to validate the value returned by INT 13h.
Further down in MSINIT.ASM, DOS
sets up the hard disks
, calling the SETHARD routine for each drive, but it will not set up more than two. Trouble will start near the
SETIT label
, where the DRVMAX variable may end up with a number much higher than the number of drives that SETHARD was run on.
Eventually, disaster strikes in the $SETDPB routine in the DOS kernel. The
code near LOG2LOOP label
attempts to calculate the cluster shift for the FAT file system, but gets stuck in an endless loop because the BPB for a drive was never initialized and contains zeros.
This bug is present in every DOS version with hard disk support before 5.0, that is, in DOS 2.0 up to and including DOS 4. In my experiments, all these DOS versions hang when booting on a machine that exposes four BIOS drives. MS-DOS 4.01 from April 1989 still hangs, and so does Russian MS-DOS 4.01 from February 1990.
It is clear that the bug went unnoticed or at least unfixed for a number of years simpl

data.title: Rust, Python, and TypeScript: the new trifecta
data.author: nromiun
data.article_summary: 文章预测Rust、Python和TypeScript将成为未来主导的编程语言，主要基于人工智能编码的兴起正在改变编程方式，向“以想法为导向的编程”转变。在这种新模式下，程序员更像首席架构师，专注于项目核心理念和设计，而将具体编码工作交给AI工具。语言选择不再仅凭个人偏好，而是基于库的可用性、性能需求和平台集成等基本因素。Rust因其高效和内存管理优势成为默认选择，Python适合机器学习，TypeScript则适用于web开发。强类型系统在“以想法为导向的编程”中尤为重要，能帮助捕捉错误并提高AI助手成功率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言的选择及未来发展，特别是在AI代码生成背景下的适用性。

不同观点：
• **[pjmlp]** 认为TypeScript团队决定用Go重写其实现并不理想，且没有计划重写V8引擎，C++插件仍然是扩展V8的最简单方式。他也不打算在操作系统脚本之外使用Python，并认为AI将使当前的语言变得不再重要，因为AI生成代码的能力在提高。
  
• **[benterix]** 指出TypeScript并非原生在浏览器中运行，批评了原评论中的不准确表述，暗示可能是由于对前端技术发展的不了解或表述不严谨。

• **[robviren]** 赞同Python和TypeScript/JavaScript在AI领域的优势，但不太确定Rust是否应被列入其中。他认为Rust的库生态不如Python，并建议如果要选第三种语言，他更倾向于Go，因为其向后兼容性强、标准库 robust，且格式严格。

• **[Tohsig]** 认为现在预测哪些语言将主导未来还为时过早，但个人经验表明，强大的类型系统确实提高了从LLM获得的响应准确性。他还观察到JS/TS代码的大量存在使得模型对这些语言的理解更准确，而对如Elixir等较小众语言的支持则不够理想。

• **[misja111]** 强调企业级服务器软件需要的是安全性、稳定性、可扩展性和易维护性，Python、TypeScript和Rust都不符合这些要求。他认为Java等垃圾回收语言在这方面更具优势，因为不需要处理如数据所有权等底层细节。

• **[sshine]** 分享了他对几种语言的编码体验，对TypeScript和Rust表示满意，但对Haskell的冗长和不美观表示失望。他提到自己不太在意代码的冗长，但不喜欢格式化问题，因此设置了预提交钩子来运行格式化工具。

• 争议焦点之一是TypeScript的实现和其在浏览器中的运行情况。
• 对Rust是否应被视为一种主流的AI开发语言存在分歧，部分评论者认为其生态不如Python和JavaScript。
• 关于AI生成代码对编程语言的影响，有观点认为现有语言可能会因为AI的进步而变得不再重要。
• 对企业级软件开发中哪种语言最适合，评论者有不同看法，主要集中在语言的安全性、稳定性和可维护性上。

44796281.article_content:
You heard it here first: my guess is that Rust, Python, and TypeScript are going to become the dominant languages going forward (excluding the mobile market, which has extra wrinkles). The argument is simple. Increasing use of AI coding is going to weaken people’s loyalty to programming languages, moving it from what is often a tribal decision to one based on fundamentals. And the fundamentals for those 3 languages look pretty strong to me: Rust targets system software or places where efficiency is paramount. Python brings a powerful ecosystem of mathematical and numerical libraries to bear and lends itself well to experimentation and prototyping. And TypeScript of course runs natively on browsers and the web and a number of other areas. And all of them, at least if setup properly, offer strong static typing and the easy use of dependencies. Let’s walk through the argument point by point.
AI is moving us towards
idea-oriented programming
Building with an LLM is presently a rather uneven experience, but I think the long-term trend is clear enough. We are seeing a shift towards a new programming paradigm. Dave Herman and I have recently taken to calling it
idea-oriented programming
. As the name suggests,
idea-oriented programming
is
programming where you are focused first and foremost on
ideas
behind your project
.
Why do I say
idea-oriented programming
and not
vibe coding
? To me, they are different beasts. Vibe coding suggests a kind of breezy indifference to the specifics – kind of waving your hand vaguely at the AI and saying “do something like this”.
That smacks of
treating the AI like a genie
– or perhaps a servant, neither of which I think is useful.
Idea-oriented programming is very much
programming
Idea-oriented programming, in contrast, is definitely
programming
. But your role is different. As the programmer, you’re more like the chief architect. Your coding tools are like your apprentices. You are thinking about the goals and the key aspects of the design. You lay out a crisp plan and delegate the heavy lifting to the tools – and then you review their output, making tweaks and, importantly, generalizing those tweaks into persistent principles. When some part of the problem gets tricky, you are rolling up your sleeves and do some hands-on debugging and problem solving.
If you’ve been in the industry a while, this description will be familiar. It’s essentially the role of a Principal Engineer. It’s also a solid description of what I think an open-source mentor ought to do.
Idea-oriented programming changes the priorities for language choice
In the past, when I built software projects, I would default to Rust. It’s not that Rust is the best choice for everything. It’s that I know Rust best, and so I move the fastest when I use it. I would only adopt a different language if it offered a compelling advantage (or of course if I just wanted to try a new language, which I do enjoy).
But when I’m buiding things with an AI assistant, I’ve found I think differently. I’m thinking more about what libraries are available, what my fundamental performance needs are, and what platforms I expect to integrate with. I want things to be as straightforward and high-level as I can get them, because that will give the AI the best chance of success and minimize my need to dig in. The result is that I wind up with a mix of Python (when I want access to machine-learning libraries), TypeScript (when I’m building a web app, VSCode Extension, or something else where the native APIs are in TypeScript), and Rust otherwise.
Why Rust as the default? Well, I like it of course, but more importantly I know that its type system will catch errors up front and I know that its overall design will result in performant code that uses relatively little memory. If I am then going to run that code in the cloud, that will lower my costs, and if I’m running it on my desktop, it’ll give more RAM for Microsoft Outlook to consume.

Type systems are hugely important for idea-oriented programming
LLMs kind of turn the tables on what we expect from a computer. Typical computers can cross-reference vast amounts of information and perform deterministic computations lightning fast, but falter with even a whiff of ambiguity. LLMs, in contrast, can be surprisingly creative and thoughtful, but they have limited awareness of things that are not right in front of their face, unless they correspond to some pattern that is ingrained from training. They’re a lot more like humans that way. 44796281.article_summary: 文章预测Rust、Python和TypeScript将成为未来主导的编程语言，主要基于人工智能编码的兴起正在改变编程方式，向“以想法为导向的编程”转变。在这种新模式下，程序员更像首席架构师，专注于项目核心理念和设计，而将具体编码工作交给AI工具。语言选择不再仅凭个人偏好，而是基于库的可用性、性能需求和平台集成等基本因素。Rust因其高效和内存管理优势成为默认选择，Python适合机器学习，TypeScript则适用于web开发。强类型系统在“以想法为导向的编程”中尤为重要，能帮助捕捉错误并提高AI助手成功率。

data.title: If you're remote, ramble
data.author: lawgimenez
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种适用于2-10人远程团队的沟通技巧：在团队聊天应用中为每个成员创建个人“闲聊”频道。这些频道让成员可以分享想法、项目建议、兴趣爱好等，而不干扰团队频道。个人频道以成员名字命名，只有本人能发布主帖，其他人可在 thread 中回复。这些频道放在列表底部，默认静音，不要求每个人都阅读。这种方法在 Obsidian 团队中试验成功，替代了会议和水 cooler 谈话，促进了创意和团队联系，同时减少干扰。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：远程工作环境中的非正式沟通渠道（如闲聊或抱怨频道）的价值和实施方式

不同观点：
• **支持创建专门的闲聊/抱怨频道**：
   - majke分享了自己在Cloudflare工作的经验，强调创建一个专门的非正式沟通渠道（如"Marek's technical corner"）能够有效解决新员工的疑问，并促进团队内部的技术讨论和文化建设。
   - rablackburn补充了远程工作中的“漫游”时间（如早晨的徒步）不仅能帮助员工区分工作与生活，还能激发创意和思考。
   - mnafees以自身在远程初创公司工作的经历，支持远程工作中的闲聊和自由发言，认为这有助于个人成长和团队学习。

• **反对强制设立闲聊频道**：
   - codingdave认为健康的讨论应自然产生，而不是通过指定的频道强制进行。他主张让团队自行组织沟通方式，而不是规定具体方法。
   - 9dev担心闲聊频道最终会变成另一个需要扫描和参与的“任务”，增加工作压力。
   - ogou因过去目睹了工作聊天中因政治、社会评论等引发的冲突和后果，决定避免参与任何非结构化的社交聊天。

• **对闲聊频道持保留态度或提出替代方案**：
   - siva7指出，没有日常会议的团队可能会从闲聊频道中获益，但对于那些已经有日常会议的团队，闲聊频道可能被视为额外任务而失败。
   - liveoneggs建议选择合适的频道组（如按团队/项目），让讨论自然发展，同时可以混合工作话题和个人兴趣分享。
   - senko认为闲聊频道与一般的非工作话题频道没有区别，对于小团队来说，一个频道比多个频道更易管理。
   - esperent表示已经对过多的聊天频道感到疲劳，但认为一个单一的闲聊频道是可以接受的。

• **特殊情况和个人经历**：
   - ryankrage77分享了团队自发创建第二聊天频道的经验，用于提问和抱怨，避免在主聊天中产生干扰。
   - marginalia_nu强调即使独自工作，记录想法和半成品思考也非常有用，能帮助捕捉稍纵即逝的创意。
   - comrade1234提到有心理健康问题的同事可能会在闲聊频道中发表大量难以理解的文字，影响沟通效果。

补充讨论：
- **领导风格对闲聊频道的影响**：softwaredoug指出，有些领导对不受控的沟通感到威胁，可能将闲聊视为“分心”或“麻烦制造者”的行为，这种环境可能抑制自由讨论。
- **文化和团队规模的影响**：skhameneh认为，健康的远程优先公司应鼓励类似“水 cooler talk”的非正式沟通，以区别于传统以办公室为中心的公司文化。

争议焦点：
- 是否应设立强制性的闲聊/抱怨频道，还是让团队自然形成沟通方式。一方认为指定频道有助于降低新员工的沟通摩擦，另一方则担心这会增加工作负担并限制自由沟通。

44775563.article_content:
If you're remote, ramble
July 31, 2025
·
1 minute read
A tip for remote teams of 2-10 people. Create a personal “ramblings” channel for each teammate in your team’s chat app of choice.
Ramblings channels let everyone share what’s on their mind without cluttering group channels. Think of them as personal journals or microblogs inside your team’s chat app, a lightweight way to add ambient social cohesion.
People typically post short updates 1-3 times per week. Common topics include:
ideas related to current projects
musings about blog posts, articles, user feedback
“what if” suggestions
photos from recent trips or hobbies
rubber ducking a problem
Each ramblings channel should be named after the team member, and only that person can post top-level messages. Others can reply in threads, but not start new ones.
All the ramblings channels should be in a
Ramblings
section at the bottom of the channel list. They should be muted by default, with no expectation that anyone else will read them.
We started experimenting with ramblings at
Obsidian
two years ago, and they’ve been surprisingly sticky. We have no scheduled meetings, so ramblings are our equivalent of water cooler talk. We want as much deep focus time as possible, so ramblings help us stay connected while minimizing interruptions.
Because they are so free and loose, some of our best ideas emerge from ramblings. They’re often the source of feature ideas, small prototypes, and creative solutions to long-standing problems.
About once a year, we do a week-long in-person meetup. Ramblings have been one successful way we keep the human connection going throughout the rest of the year.

data.title: Mastercard deflects blame for NSFW games being taken down
data.author: croes
data.article_summary: Valve和Itch.io在压力下从平台移除了部分NSFW游戏，最初报道称是由于信用卡公司施压。然而，万事达卡（Mastercard）发布声明否认直接责任，称其仅提供支付技术与网络，允许所有合法购买，但要求商户防止非法购买。尽管如此，Valve表示支付处理方引用了万事达卡的规则5.12.7，并指出其对品牌风险的影响，最终导致游戏下架。尽管万事达卡声称未直接干预，但其影响似乎通过支付处理方间接体现。此事引发了对信用卡公司和平台内容审核政策的广泛讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mastercard在处理合法但可能影响其品牌形象的交易时的规则和行为，以及支付处理公司在内容审查中的角色。

不同观点：
• rob74：质疑Mastercard声明中的矛盾，一方面声称允许所有合法购买，另一方面其规则5.12.7又赋予公司拒绝可能损害其声誉的交易的权力，认为规则模糊不清。
• cedws：批评Mastercard和Visa在支付处理市场的双头垄断，认为这些公司不应拥有如此大的金融控制权，并主张对其进行更严格的监管。
• kmfrk：补充文章标题未完全传达的信息，指出Valve称支付处理公司特别提到Mastercard的规则导致了NSFW游戏的下架。
• roenxi：认为Mastercard的声明可能是真实的，但对其进行问责仍然是有必要的，因为它们对监管机构的影响力最大。
• phendrenad2：认为问题的根源在于支付公司的投资者，他们受到负面新闻活动的影响，试图将世界“迪士尼化”，使得公司采取过于保守的内容审查政策。
• nottorp：认为Mastercard在发现大量游戏玩家对其决定不满后，正试图进行损害控制。
• jug：质疑为何信用卡公司会在意其处理的合法交易是否影响其形象，认为信用卡公司应仅关注其金融功能。
• nottorp：（补充）指出亚马逊也在处理包含强奸场景的电影，质疑Mastercard为何区别对待。
• makeitdouble：惊讶于Mastercard规则的宽泛，认为公司可以根据自己的判断拒绝任何可能影响其声誉的交易，即使这些交易是合法的。
• mitthrowaway2：对NSFW标签用于视频游戏表示幽默评论，指出其他视频游戏并未被如此标签。
• lesuorac：不认为处理合法支付会给支付处理公司带来声誉风险，质疑那些写信投诉的人的观点。
• calibas：批评Mastercard规则的模糊性和执行的随意性，认为公司可以随意创建和执行规则。
• jajuuka：认为Mastercard在推卸责任，指出除非有新的法规，否则Visa和Mastercard将继续随意行使他们的权力。
• polytely：建议Valve可以考虑成为自己的支付处理商，利用其资金实力和技术背景来规避当前问题。
• rs186：提出一个假设性问题，询问如果Steam仅接受现金或加密货币支付，是否可以规避当前问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到支付处理市场的垄断性和缺乏竞争，以及由此带来的监管需求。
• 对Mastercard规则的模糊性和执行的随意性存在广泛批评，认为这赋予公司过大的权力。
• 部分评论关注问题的根源，认为投资者的压力和负面新闻活动是导致支付公司采取保守政策的原因。
• 有建议提出通过技术手段（如加密货币）或法规来规避当前支付处理公司带来的问题。

争议焦点：
• Mastercard是否应根据其主观判断拒绝可能影响其声誉的合法交易。
• 支付处理公司在内容审查中的角色和其规则的合理性与合法性。
• 如何在保持市场自由的同时，对支付处理公司进行有效监管。

44783566.article_content:
(Image credit: Getty Images)
Two weeks after Valve confirmed it had
removed a pile of NSFW games from Steam
because of pressure from credit card companies—and one week after
Itch.io followed suit
—Mastercard has
released a statement
denying responsibility for the takedowns, saying it "allows all lawful purchases" to be processed through its systems.
"Mastercard has not evaluated any game or required restrictions of any activity on game creator sites and platforms, contrary to media reports and allegations," the company says
.
"Our payment network follows standards based on the rule of law. Put simply, we allow all lawful purchases on our network. At the same time, we require merchants to have appropriate controls to ensure Mastercard cards cannot be used for unlawful purchases, including illegal adult content."
Related articles
Valve confirms credit card companies pressured it to delist certain adult games from Steam
Itch.io deindexes NSFW games after becoming the latest target of skittish credit card companies and anti-porn group Collective Shout
'Dangerous on a whole new level'—while Steam's policy change is new, the shadow of credit card meddling has been looming for a while, with Nier: Automata's Yoko Taro sounding the alarm last year
It's an odd statement at first glance, because while the content removed by Steam and Itch.io may violate laws in some countries, it's fully legal in the US—objectionable and gross as hell in some cases, sure, but still within the boundaries of the law. Apart from that, both Valve and Itch.io explicitly stated that payment processors are the reason games were deindexed or removed from sale entirely.
Mastercard's 'out' here seems to be found in the structure of its operations. The company's website says it is "neither an issuer [a merchant bank] nor an acquirer [a bank, credit union, or other entity that provides debit cards or lines of credit to consumers]," but rather that it "
provide[s] the technology and the network that power transactions
." In other words, Mastercard does not process payments, it facilitates the systems that do.
In the case of Itch.io, the platform specifies in its "
update on NSFW content
" that its payment processors are Paypal and Stripe—and Stripe, which supports a
range of payment methods
including Visa and Mastercards, was the one
Itch.io
"suspended the ability to pay with for 18+ content for the foreseeable future."
Similarly, both
Verotel
and
CCBill
, which were recently recommended by the IGDA as "alternatives to overly risk-averse financial partners," accept major credit cards as payment methods.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
In a statement provided to PC Gamer, Valve said that it had tried to work things out with Mastercard directly prior to removing the games, and suggested that Mastercard did have at least an indirect influence on the outcome.
"Mastercard did not communicate with Valve directly, despite our request to do so," a Valve representative said. "Mastercard communicated with payment processors and their acquiring banks. Payment processors communicated this with Valve, and we replied by outlining Steam’s policy since 2018 of attempting to distribute games that are legal for distribution.
"Payment processors rejected this, and specifically cited Mastercard’s Rule 5.12.7 and risk to the Mastercard brand."
"Mastercard did not communicate with Valve directly, despite our request to do so."
Valve representative
Mastercard's Rule 5.12.7
relates to "illegal or brand-damaging transactions," and states:
A Merchant must not submit to its Acquirer, and a Customer must not submit to the Interchange System, any Transaction that is illegal, or in the sole discretion of the Corporation, may damage the goodwill of the Corporation or reflect negatively on the Marks.

44783566.article_summary: Valve和Itch.io在压力下从平台移除了部分NSFW游戏，最初报道称是由于信用卡公司施压。然而，万事达卡（Mastercard）发布声明否认直接责任，称其仅提供支付技术与网络，允许所有合法购买，但要求商户防止非法购买。尽管如此，Valve表示支付处理方引用了万事达卡的规则5.12.7，并指出其对品牌风险的影响，最终导致游戏下架。尽管万事达卡声称未直接干预，但其影响似乎通过支付处理方间接体现。此事引发了对信用卡公司和平台内容审核政策的广泛讨论。
44783566.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mastercard在处理合法但可能影响其品牌形象的交易时的规则和行为，以及支付处理公司在内容审查中的角色。

不同观点：
• rob74：质疑Mastercard声明中的矛盾，一方面声称允许所有合法购买，另一方面其规则5.12.7又赋予公司拒绝可能损害其声誉的交易的权力，认为规则模糊不清。
• cedws：批评Mastercard和Visa在支付处理市场的双头垄断，认为这些公司不应拥有如此大的金融控制权，并主张对其进行更严格的监管。
• kmfrk：补充文章标题未完全传达的信息，指出Valve称支付处理公司特别提到Mastercard的规则导致了NSFW游戏的下架。
• roenxi：认为Mastercard的声明可能是真实的，但对其进行问责仍然是有必要的，因为它们对监管机构的影响力最大。
• phendrenad2：认为问题的根源在于支付公司的投资者，他们受到负面新闻活动的影响，试图将世界“迪士尼化”，使得公司采取过于保守的内容审查政策。
• nottorp：认为Mastercard在发现大量游戏玩家对其决定不满后，正试图进行损害控制。
• jug：质疑为何信用卡公司会在意其处理的合法交易是否影响其形象，认为信用卡公司应仅关注其金融功能。
• nottorp：（补充）指出亚马逊也在处理包含强奸场景的电影，质疑Mastercard为何区别对待。
• makeitdouble：惊讶于Mastercard规则的宽泛，认为公司可以根据自己的判断拒绝任何可能影响其声誉的交易，即使这些交易是合法的。
• mitthrowaway2：对NSFW标签用于视频游戏表示幽默评论，指出其他视频游戏并未被如此标签。
• lesuorac：不认为处理合法支付会给支付处理公司带来声誉风险，质疑那些写信投诉的人的观点。
• calibas：批评Mastercard规则的模糊性和执行的随意性，认为公司可以随意创建和执行规则。
• jajuuka：认为Mastercard在推卸责任，指出除非有新的法规，否则Visa和Mastercard将继续随意行使他们的权力。
• polytely：建议Valve可以考虑成为自己的支付处理商，利用其资金实力和技术背景来规避当前问题。
• rs186：提出一个假设性问题，询问如果Steam仅接受现金或加密货币支付，是否可以规避当前问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到支付处理市场的垄断性和缺乏竞争，以及由此带来的监管需求。
• 对Mastercard规则的模糊性和执行的随意性存在广泛批评，认为这赋予公司过大的权力。
• 部分评论关注问题的根源，认为投资者的压力和负面新闻活动是导致支付公司采取保守政策的原因。
• 有建议提出通过技术手段（如加密货币）或法规来规避当前支付处理公司带来的问题。

争议焦点：
• Mastercard是否应根据其主观判断拒绝可能影响其声誉的合法交易。
• 支付处理公司在内容审查中的角色和其规则的合理性与合法性。
• 如何在保持市场自由的同时，对支付处理公司进行有效监管。

data.title: This Old SGI: notes and memoirs on the Silicon Graphics 4D series (1996)
data.author: exvi
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是A. J. Corda编写的关于其修复和维护SGI 4D系列机器的经验笔记，包含详细的操作指南和技术细节。主要内容包括：SGI系统和部件的来源、CDC重贴牌的SGI系统、IRIX平台支持笔记、4D系列串口 pinout、光盘启动和软件安装、获取root权限的方法、硬盘格式化和系统恢复、PROM监控命令和环境变量、图形和硬件配置、电源和散热问题、实时时钟和非易失性内存问题、硬件调试技巧等。文章还分享了作者在Usenet上寻求帮助的经验，强调在未获及时回复时应重新审视问题，而不是立即重发帖子，许多问题可以通过重新阅读文档或重新思考解决方法来解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对SGI工作站及其影响力的回顾与设想

不同观点：
• lastdong：认为Nvidia让人们在家中拥有相当于SGI级别机器的能力，并对之前HN上的讨论进行了引用，暗示技术进步令人难以置信。
• JSR_FDED：分享了自己拥有并修复Indigo2 Max Impact工作站的经历，强调该设备在当时的高价值和4Dwm桌面的现代适用性。
• fidotron：提到了自己获得的4D/60 "buttons box"，讨论了该设备的稀有性和与现代设备接口的困难，还分享了与电力供应相关的趣闻。
• t1234s：称赞O2工作站的设计巧妙，尤其是其组件易于更换的特点。
• aa-jv：回忆了自己的第一台"真正的电脑"MIPS Magnum pizzabox RC3230，并升级到SGI Indy，表达了对SGI品牌的热爱。同时，提出一个假设性问题：如果SGI当年制造了笔记本电脑，生活会怎样不同，特别是与苹果的tiBook对比。

补充讨论：
• fidotron提到设备的接口困难和电力需求问题，反映出旧设备在现代环境中的适应性挑战。
• aa-jv对SGI未实现的笔记本电脑设想的讨论引发了对技术发展路径的另一种历史可能性思考，特别是与苹果产品的对比，增加了讨论的深度。

争议焦点：
• 不同设备的历史价值和技术影响在用户间的体验和评价存在差异，比如对Indigo2和O2工作站的个人情感和使用体验。
• SGI是否能制造出成功的笔记本电脑，这一假设引发了对技术发展方向和市场竞争的讨论。

Introduction
I am posting this assortment of notes and observations as
a kind of "thank you" to the numerous people who have replied
to my posts in the past.  The free flow of information is
the life-blood of the internet community, and this is my feeble
attempt to maintain that flow, while at the same time repaying
the kindness shown me by other members of the community in my
rather obsessive attempts to revive a defunct 4D professional
series machine.
I have posted a number of messages concerning my project, and
I can say that all the replies I have received have been quite
helpful. One of the things you learn early on as a denizen of
the net is the utility of Usenet posts. You also learn that
the volume of answers can convey almost as much information
as the content of those answers. If I post a question and
receive a significant number of replies, then I can be relatively
certain that others have run across (and possibly solved) the
same class of problem. If, however, I receive no responses, it
indicates that this is a new problem not previously encountered
(quite unlikely, due to the age of the equipment in this case),
the problem represents a true hardware-level failure (usually
at the IC level) or the problem is due to some fundamental stupidity
on my part (by far the most likely scenario!). This means that
it's time to re-evaluate the procedure which caused the problem,
which usually leads to an alternate approach which inevitably
works. During this project, I have only had 2 genuine hardware
failures, both of which had very little usenet response. The
rest of the low-response questions were solved by re-reading
the documentation available, or using my common sense when
it was at last evident that this was not a common bug.
The point of this diatribe is that if you don't receive an
immediate response to a usenet post, don't immediately repost
it! Think the problem out. If none of the other half-million or so
people who have seen your post have run across your particular
problem, then the odds are that it's due to some fundamental
mistake or misunderstanding on your part. Step back and

data.title: No Comment (2010)
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了21世纪编程的核心在于实现想法，而非单纯追求技术。作者解释不开放评论的原因是为了避免负面技术讨论带来的影响，并分享了自己在编程初期的经验：面对看似不合理的代码时，发现深入了解背景和问题复杂性很重要。作者批评了工程师常有的草率批评态度，并以Flickr为例，强调积极的在线社区体验，认为应专注于分享实际经验而非无谓争辩。文章最后指出，编程讨论不应沉迷于技术争论，而应关注更有意义的交流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：线上评论文化的优缺点及评论功能的价值

不同观点：
• **评论文化倾向于攻击性**：[getnormality] 指出，线上评论往往聚焦于挑错，试图证明原帖（OP）错误、无知或不合逻辑，而不是提供有见地的反馈。这种现象普遍存在，且人们往往没有意识到自己也在这样做。

• **私人交流 vs. 公开评论**：[dcminter] 通过引用侦探小说《Gaudy Night》中的一段对话，说明评论区往往引发强烈的情感反应，而私人信件交流则更为合适。评论区的公开性质容易导致过度批评，而非建设性反馈。

• **评论区的实用性与管理困难**：[stillpointlab] 和 [Brajeshwar] 提到，他们因为垃圾邮件和不良互动体验关闭了博客的评论功能。[stillpointlab] 还指出，现代网络评论往往受外部动机驱动，导致更多毒性。相比之下，[amitp] 认为评论区提供了很多有价值的信息和反馈，且通过外包管理（如 Disqus）可以有效减少管理负担。

• **评论区的价值与特定场景下的必要性**：[bombcar] 提到低流量博客的评论区可能包含对特定问题的唯一解决方案。[amitp] 强调评论区对他个人的学习与知识补充有很大帮助，并将其比作会议后的提问环节，具有潜在价值。

• **评论功能的设计与管理责任**：[Arch-TK] 指出，设计决策需要有详细文档支持，以避免依赖口头交流。这暗示了评论或文档的必要性。[taeric] 则认为，拥有评论区意味着要承担管理责任，防止滥用，而这可能增加负担。

补充讨论：
• **社交媒体与邮件反馈**：[thibaultamartin] 选择不在博客中嵌入评论，而是通过社交媒体和邮件获取反馈，认为这样能获得更有质量的互动。

• **评论区的争议性与网络对立现象**：[dsotm17] 提到，评论区常有“反对一切”的对立者，无论原帖内容如何，都会被挑错和反对，这种“反对主义”加剧了网络对立。

• **博客文化的变迁与短文趋势**：[LAC-Tech] 怀念过去的博客文化，认为短小精悍的文章更符合读者需求，并影响了他自己的写作风格。

争议焦点：评论区的价值与管理难题。一方认为评论区提供了有价值的互动和反馈，另一方则认为评论区容易引发无建设性的批评和不良互动，管理负担重且效果不佳。

44798434.article_content:
programming in the
twenty-first century
It's not about technology for its own sake. It's about being able to implement your ideas.
No Comment
I received a few emails after
last time
along the lines of "Oh. Perl. Homebrew CMS.
That's
why you don't allow people to post comments." Well, no, but it was definitely a conscious decision. The Web 2.0 answer is that I'm outsourcing comments to
reddit
and
Hacker News
. The real reason is this:
The negativity of online technical discussions makes me bitter, and even though I'm sometimes drawn to them I need to stay away.
To be fair, this isn't true only of technical discussions. Back when I was on
Usenet
, I took refuge from geeky bickering in a group about cooking...only to find people arguing the merits of
Miracle Whip
versus mayonnaise. Put enough people together and there are sure to be complaints and conflicting personal agendas. But with smart, technically-oriented people, I'd expect there to be more sharing of real experiences, but that's often not the case.
Here's a lesson I learned very early on after I started working full-time as a programmer (and that's a peculiar sentence for me to read, as I no longer program for a living). I'd be looking at some code at my desk, and it made no sense. Why would anyone write it like this? There's an obvious and cleaner way to approach the same problem.
So I'd go down the hall to the person who wrote it in the first place and start asking questions...and find out that I didn't have the whole picture, the problem was messier than it first appeared, and there were perfectly valid reasons for the code being that way. This happened again and again. Sometimes I did find a real flaw, but even then it may have only occurred with data that wasn't actually possible (because, for example, it was filtered by another part of the system). Talking face to face changed everything, because they could draw diagrams, pull out specs, and give concrete examples.
I think that initial knee-jerk "I've been looking at this for ten seconds and now let me explain the critical flaws" reaction is a common one among people with engineering mindsets. And that's not a good thing. I've seen this repeatedly, from people putting down programming languages for silly, superficial reasons (Perl's sigils, Python's enforced indentation), to ridiculous off-the-cuff put downs of new products (such as the predictions of doom in the
Slashdot announcement
of the original iPod in 2001).
The online community that I've had the most overwhelmingly positive experience with is the photo-sharing site
Flickr
. I'll keep talking about Flickr, because it played a big part in getting me out of some ruts, and I've seen more great photographs over the last five years than I would have seen in ten lifetimes otherwise. I know that if you dig around you can find tedious rants from equipment collectors, but I do a good job of avoiding those. I don't think I've ever seen real negativity in photo comments other than suggestions for different crops or the occasional technical criticisms. There are so many good photos to see that there's no reason to waste time with ones the don't appeal to me. That's supported by only allowing up-voting of photos (by adding a shot to your favorites); there's no way to formally register dislike.
Flickr gets my time, but most of the programming discussion sites don't.

data.author: ashton314
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大语言模型（LLM）生成文本的缺陷，特别是当读者误以为这些文本是由人类撰写时产生的不适感。作者指出，机器生成的文本往往包含过多无意义的赘述，缺乏人类作者的意图和用心，导致读者在理解文本时感到困惑和疲惫。尽管LLM在工程上是一项壮举，可以解决许多复杂问题，但它们无法替代人类的创造力和情感。文章还提到，尽管人们可能会依赖LLM作弊或寻求虚假的情感连接，但这些机器终究无法取代人类的思想和价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）生成内容的质量及其使用场景的合理性

不同观点：
• **LLM生成内容多为无意义的内容填充**：[lordnacho] 认为LLM生成的很多文档类似于没有实际内容的“填充物”，例如餐馆菜单、部分商业报告等。虽然形式上看似完整，但缺乏核心思想，只能在不需要深入理解的情况下使用。
  
• **LLM作为辅助工具而非替代者**：[stillpointlab] 表示LLM可以作为辅助工具，用于检查语法或提供反馈，但不适合完全替代人类写作。当LLM重写段落时，会出现让读者不适的“生硬感”。

• **LLM生成质量依赖于提示的详细程度**：[ozgung] 提出LLM生成的内容质量与输入提示的详细程度密切相关。过短的提示会导致内容空洞，而过长的提示则会使LLM失去其作为辅助工具的优势。

• **LLM在特定场景下具有高效性**：[josephjrobison] 认为LLM在提高效率方面有显著优势，尤其是在内容整理、格式化以及结合搜索功能时。同时，LLM在娱乐内容生成方面也有其价值，尽管可能不如艺术作品那样有深度。

• **LLM生成内容可能缺乏人类意图**：[fleebee] 指出，LLM生成的内容缺乏人类作者的隐含意图，导致读者在理解时感到不适。这种缺乏社会契约的沟通让LLM内容显得“空洞”。

• **LLM可用于改进低质量的人类文档**：[PeterStuer] 认为，许多设计文档如果由LLM生成可能会更好，因为原本的文档质量可能已经很低。LLM的使用效果取决于操作者，而非工具本身。

• **低输入生成内容等同于垃圾信息**：[blargey] 强调，低质量的输入会导致LLM生成大量无意义的“填充内容”，这些内容在正式沟通中毫无价值，类似于“垃圾信息”。

补充讨论：
• **对LLM生成内容的抵触情绪**：[yapyap] 和 [parpfish] 都提到，如果被迫阅读由LLM生成且质量低劣的长文档，会感到愤怒和浪费时间。这种情绪在工作场景中尤为明显。

• **LLM的不断改进**：[eru] 认为，作者在抱怨LLM不够好，但LLM在不断进步。尽管目前可能存在问题，但未来会得到改善。

• **标题和链接诱导性问题**：[dang] 关注文章标题的准确性和中立性，认为需要避免使用诱导性语言。

争议焦点：
• **LLM生成内容的质量和实用性**：一方认为LLM生成的内容多为无意义填充，另一方则认为LLM是有效的辅助工具，关键在于如何使用。

44797917.article_content:
Contents
AI stands for “Artificial Inanity”
4 Aug 2025
Writing
There’s something icky about LLM-generated text when you think it’s written by a human. I think I finally put my finger on one reason why I feel this way.
Note on the title: “Artificial Inanity” comes from Neal Stephenson’s novel
Anathem
.
At work I was sent a long design document and asked for my thoughts on it. As I read, I had a really hard time following it. Eventually I guessed correctly (confirmed via a follow-up conversation I had with the “author”
I have “author” in quotes because, if a machine wrote it, you don’t merit being called the
author
of the work.
) that an LLM had generated the majority of the document. Parts of it
sounded
like a decent design document, but there was just way too much fluff that served only to confuse me.
When I read technical documents, I read to understand the content. In this mode of reading, I operate under the assumption that the author had a reason for choosing the words they did, and that every sentence is there to convey something that the author wishes me to understand.
This mode fails when an LLM or the like has generated the text. When I read something I know came out of a computer’s probabilistic sampling of a token-space, I have read knowing that every statement might be some hallucinated slop or incidental filler. I
cannot
trust that the human operator’s intent is expressed by the machine. In fact, I am confident that it is often
not
, but I have to waste tremendous effort trying to find that gap. Reading slop text when I think I’m reading real text is exhausting: since I am not on the alert for hallucinations or irrelevancies, every turn of phrase that seems out of place causes me to wonder
why that phrase it there
and
what am I missing
when in reality, such questions are ill formed: that was just a phrase composed by accident that
sounds
good but actually is devoid of much intent at all.
Intent
is the core thing: the
lack
of intent is what makes reading AI-slop so revolting. There needs to be a human intent—human will and human care—behind everything that is demanded of our care and attention. Even if you agree with Rolland Barthes’
The author of
The Death of the Author
, an essay where Barthes argues that focusing on the author’s intent is fruitless—the meaning of a text is the effect it has on the audience.
views on literary criticism, the fact that there
is
an author who put care and intent into a work imbues that work with infinitely more meaning than if it were spat out by a machine.
Counterfeits to human connection will—unfortunately—always be in demand. The multi-billion dollar industry churning out pornography is proof enough. People will probably always, from here on out, be using LLMs to cheat their way through classes and themselves out of learning. Some might turn to them for some faux-companionship. Others will be prompting themselves to death by offloading more and more of their reasoning to machines, convinced that the computer—like a slot machine—somehow will let them win bigger in life.
I am
not
saying that LLMs are worthless—they are marvels of engineering and can solve some particularly thorny problems that have confounded us for decades. But it’s important to remember that, no matter how capable these machines get, they are not humans. And no human is so worthless as to be replaceable with a machine.

data.title: Genie 3: A new frontier for world models
data.author: bradleyg223
data.article_summary: 《Genie 3：世界模型的新前沿》一文介绍了Google DeepMind开发的Genie 3模型，这是一个通用世界模型，能够生成多样化的互动环境。给定文本提示，Genie 3可以以每秒24帧的速率实时生成动态世界，保持数分钟的一致性，分辨率为720p。该模型是世界模拟领域的重要进展，支持实时交互，并提升了先前模型Genie 1和Genie 2的 consistency（一致性）和realism（真实性）。Genie 3能够模拟物理属性、自然现象、复杂环境交互，以及生成生态系统和动物行为。其应用包括训练AI代理在丰富模拟环境中学习，推动人工通用智能（AGI）的发展。文章还展示了多个实际视频示例，如火山地形导航、水上摩托节日、飓风中的佛罗里达道路等场景。

不同观点：
• **对技术进步的惊叹**：
   - modeless 对 Genie 3 的实时运行能力和一致性表示惊讶，认为这是未来世界模型在机器人学和现实世界AI中重要作用的预兆。
   - Oarch 和 Ollin 也对技术进步表示震惊，Ollin 还提供了技术细节的推测，例如 VAE 的使用和帧间互动延迟。

• **对技术取代人类创造力的担忧**：
   - timeattack 表达了对生成式AI取代人类创造力的担忧，认为这会剥夺人类的创造价值，并对未来的经济和社会影响表示悲观。
   - brotchie 感受到了一种解离感，担心当前现实可能是未来自我或某种意识生活在AI生成的环境中的结果。

• **对技术应用前景的期待**：
   - arjie 认为 Genie 3 可以扩展人们对历史和科学的视角，创造沉浸式体验，并回忆童年时对类似技术的惊叹。
   - jimmySixDOF 期待这项技术与增强现实（XR）头显结合，创造出与AI互动的全新方式。

• **对技术细节和局限性的讨论**：
   - Tejas D. Kulkarni 在推文中指出了 Genie 3 的局限性，包括物理模拟困难、多智能体互动复杂、指令执行失败等。
   - Bjorkbat 认为这些世界模型更像是视频游戏模拟器，而非真正的世界模拟器，因为它们通常从第一人称或第三人称视角展示，且局限于游戏情境。

• **对商业化和研究模式的批评**：
   - addisonj 批评了当前AI领域从学术研究快速转向商业化提取价值的趋势，担心这会影响长期的科研和政策制定。
   - demirbey05 认为这种AI应用是计算资源的浪费，特别是在科学研究更需要计算能力的情况下，并对环境影响表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• **对未来技术发展的期待与质疑**：
   - yanis_t 提到文本渲染问题曾经在图像AI中存在，但很快被解决，暗示当前技术的局限性可能会迅速得到改善。
   - Workaccount2 期待Genie 3 技术与VR结合，创造出更具沉浸感的体验，但对谷歌的商业化速度表示失望。

争议焦点：
• 技术进步带来的创造力取代和经济影响是主要争议点。一方认为生成式AI会剥夺人类的创造价值，另一方则期待这些技术能带来新的沉浸式体验和应用前景。
• 技术细节和应用范围的局限性也被讨论，特别是物理模拟和多智能体互动的复杂性。

总体而言，评论中充满了对Genie 3技术进步的惊叹和对未来应用前景的期待，同时也伴随着对技术取代人类创造力和经济影响的担忧。技术细节和商业化趋势也是讨论的重要方面。

Models
Genie 3: A new frontier for world models
Published
5 August 2025
Authors
Jack Parker-Holder and Shlomi Fruchter
Share
Copy link
×
Today we are announcing Genie 3
,
a general purpose world model that can generate an unprecedented diversity of interactive environments.
Given a text prompt, Genie 3 can generate dynamic worlds that you can navigate in real time at 24 frames per second, retaining consistency for a few minutes at a resolution of 720p.
Watch
Towards world simulation
At Google DeepMind, we have been pioneering research in simulated environments for over a decade, from training agents to
master real-time strategy games
to developing simulated environments for
open-ended learning
and
robotics
. This work motivated our development of world models, which are AI systems that can use their understanding of the world to simulate aspects of it, enabling agents to predict both how an environment will evolve and how their actions will affect it.
World models are also a key stepping stone on the path to AGI, since they make it possible to train AI agents in an unlimited curriculum of rich simulation environments. Last year we introduced the first foundation world models with
Genie 1
and
Genie 2
, which could generate new environments for agents. We have also continued to push the state of the art in video generation with our models Veo 2 and Veo 3, which exhibit a deep understanding of intuitive physics.
Each of these models marks progress along different capabilities of world simulation. Genie 3 is our first world model to allow interaction in real-time, while also improving consistency and realism compared to Genie 2.

44798166.article_summary: 《Genie 3：世界模型的新前沿》一文介绍了Google DeepMind开发的Genie 3模型，这是一个通用世界模型，能够生成多样化的互动环境。给定文本提示，Genie 3可以以每秒24帧的速率实时生成动态世界，保持数分钟的一致性，分辨率为720p。该模型是世界模拟领域的重要进展，支持实时交互，并提升了先前模型Genie 1和Genie 2的 consistency（一致性）和realism（真实性）。Genie 3能够模拟物理属性、自然现象、复杂环境交互，以及生成生态系统和动物行为。其应用包括训练AI代理在丰富模拟环境中学习，推动人工通用智能（AGI）的发展。文章还展示了多个实际视频示例，如火山地形导航、水上摩托节日、飓风中的佛罗里达道路等场景。

主要讨论点：Genie 3 世界模型的技术进展及其潜在应用和影响

不同观点：
• **对技术进步的惊叹**：
   - modeless 对 Genie 3 的实时运行能力和一致性表示惊讶，认为这是未来世界模型在机器人学和现实世界AI中重要作用的预兆。
   - Oarch 和 Ollin 也对技术进步表示震惊，Ollin 还提供了技术细节的推测，例如 VAE 的使用和帧间互动延迟。

• **对技术取代人类创造力的担忧**：
   - timeattack 表达了对生成式AI取代人类创造力的担忧，认为这会剥夺人类的创造价值，并对未来的经济和社会影响表示悲观。
   - brotchie 感受到了一种解离感，担心当前现实可能是未来自我或某种意识生活在AI生成的环境中的结果。

• **对技术应用前景的期待**：
   - arjie 认为 Genie 3 可以扩展人们对历史和科学的视角，创造沉浸式体验，并回忆童年时对类似技术的惊叹。
   - jimmySixDOF 期待这项技术与增强现实（XR）头显结合，创造出与AI互动的全新方式。

• **对技术细节和局限性的讨论**：
   - Tejas D. Kulkarni 在推文中指出了 Genie 3 的局限性，包括物理模拟困难、多智能体互动复杂、指令执行失败等。
   - Bjorkbat 认为这些世界模型更像是视频游戏模拟器，而非真正的世界模拟器，因为它们通常从第一人称或第三人称视角展示，且局限于游戏情境。

• **对商业化和研究模式的批评**：
   - addisonj 批评了当前AI领域从学术研究快速转向商业化提取价值的趋势，担心这会影响长期的科研和政策制定。
   - demirbey05 认为这种AI应用是计算资源的浪费，特别是在科学研究更需要计算能力的情况下，并对环境影响表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• **对未来技术发展的期待与质疑**：
   - yanis_t 提到文本渲染问题曾经在图像AI中存在，但很快被解决，暗示当前技术的局限性可能会迅速得到改善。
   - Workaccount2 期待Genie 3 技术与VR结合，创造出更具沉浸感的体验，但对谷歌的商业化速度表示失望。

争议焦点：
• 技术进步带来的创造力取代和经济影响是主要争议点。一方认为生成式AI会剥夺人类的创造价值，另一方则期待这些技术能带来新的沉浸式体验和应用前景。
• 技术细节和应用范围的局限性也被讨论，特别是物理模拟和多智能体互动的复杂性。

总体而言，评论中充满了对Genie 3技术进步的惊叹和对未来应用前景的期待，同时也伴随着对技术取代人类创造力和经济影响的担忧。技术细节和商业化趋势也是讨论的重要方面。

主要讨论点：美国国家安全场所（NNSS）的新加速器项目Scorpius及其动态成像能力，特别是其时间分辨率和应用。

不同观点：
• bombela质疑文章中提到的"7mths"是否为笔误，并认为100纳秒的时间分辨率并不特别，因为YouTube上有人展示过纳秒甚至皮秒级别的时间分辨率。
• LAsteNERD详细介绍了洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室的高速成像能力，包括pRad、DARHT和在开发中的Scorpius项目，强调这些技术能够以极高的时间精度分析爆炸事件。
• meager_wikis对由于预算削减和裁员，这些研究项目是否能持续表示担忧。
• tandr和dez11de以调侃的方式要求看到爆炸的图片，以证实文章所述。
• getpost提到MIT曾展示过每秒10^12帧的技术，虽然应用不同，但时间分辨率更高。
• cco批评科学传播者未能提供读者希望看到的爆炸图片，认为这是吸引读者注意力的关键。
• nxobject推测这项研究可能与"无实际核武器的核弹头研究"有关。
• paradox460提到DARHT项目与此相关，建议进一步了解。
• amelius关心这些图像是否与模拟结果相符。
• avodonosov询问这些图像是否可以公开获取。
• sci-designer对技术能够达到十亿分之一秒的精度表示惊叹。
• throwaway290以"Error 404"暗示可能无法找到相关信息或图片。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是文章中提到的时间分辨率是否特别，以及为何没有提供相关图片。
• 另一个讨论点是这些高精度成像技术在实际应用中的可持续性和可访问性，特别是考虑到预算和保密问题。
• 部分评论者对图像是否公开以及是否与模拟结果相符表示关注。

data.title: AI is not Making Engineers 10x as Productive
data.author: coltonv
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了作者对AI提升工程师生产力至10倍的宣传感到的焦虑和怀疑。尽管社交媒体上充斥着类似说法，声称不使用AI的工程师将会落后，但作者的亲身实验显示，当前的AI工具在编码方面表现“尚可”，主要擅长生成样板代码，而在处理复杂项目、保持代码标准和安全性方面仍有不足。作者指出，学会使用AI工具并不困难，且AI的迅速进步可能使当前的学习很快过时。文章最后强调，所谓的10倍生产力更多是宣传，而非现实，并提醒读者不应被这种焦虑左右。作者通过实验和反思，最终摆脱了“AI 10倍工程师”的冒充者综合症。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件开发中的实际生产力提升效果，尤其是关于“10x工程师”和LLM（大型语言模型）是否能带来10倍效率提升的争议。

不同观点：
• simonw: 认为LLM能提升2-5倍的编码效率，但整体工作效率提升不到20%，10x的说法不现实。他指出软件开发的瓶颈使得整体生产力无法达到10倍提升。
• swader999: 引用文章观点，认为“10x工程师”存在，但其价值更多体现在预防不必要的工作、谈判和技术投资上，而不是纯粹的编码速度。
• generalizations: 认为普通工程师常低估AI的潜力，如果能理解AI的限制和技术复杂性，AI可以有效完成特定任务，特别是在模块化开发中。
• Glyptodon: 不认为自己是10x工程师，认为系统设计和需求分析的能力比使用AI更重要，AI不能解决过度复杂化的问题。
• bicx: 分享使用Claude Code的经验，发现整体生产力提升30%，在特定任务上（如新功能开发、代码重构）有显著提升，但在处理逻辑问题和状态修复时效果不佳。
• megaloblasto: AI帮助解决了困扰多日的bug，虽然不认为自己是10x工程师，但AI确实能显著提升特定任务的效率。
• simpaticoder: 认为LLM在“放大细节”时效果更好，能帮助学习新技术，但总体效果取决于工作任务的分布。
• siva7: 认为使用AI后代码差异（diff）变得更大，但没有更多时间进行审查。
• jf22: 认为通过良好的提示和规则设置，LLM生成的代码质量可以高于手写代码，且附带额外的代码质量提升。
• izzydata: 认为开发工作的瓶颈不在代码输入速度，而在研究、规划和明确需求，LLM带来的时间节省有限，且存在“幻觉”风险。
• neom: 分享了一个月内团队使用AI的链接，未详细说明具体效果。
• lightweb: 认为LLM在DevOps和基础设施代码上仍不理想，特别是在处理硬件、操作系统和软件交叉问题时缺乏足够的上下文。
• tptacek: 认为文章设定了不现实的10倍提升标准，并将AI支持者分类为三类，但抱怨“幻觉”问题本身说明了LLM的局限性。
• bilsbie: 认为AI让自己变得“无限生产力”，因为没有AI不会开始项目，AI帮助处理了大量繁琐的工作，使工作更有趣。

补充讨论：
• 10x工程师的存在与定义：部分评论认为10x工程师的价值体现在预防不必要的工作和提供技术指导，而不是纯粹的编码效率。
• AI在不同任务上的表现差异：一些用户发现LLM在特定任务（如代码重构、新功能开发）上表现优异，但在处理复杂逻辑问题和状态修复时效果不佳。
• LLM生成代码的质量问题：部分评论认为通过良好的提示和规则设置，LLM可以生成高质量代码，但也有评论指出LLM存在“幻觉”和生成不符合标准的代码的问题。
• AI对整体生产力的影响：多数评论认为AI能提升特定任务的效率，但对整体生产力的提升效果有限，瓶颈在于软件开发的其他环节（如需求分析、系统设计）。

争议焦点：
• LLM是否能带来10倍的生产力提升：多数评论认为10x的说法不现实，整体生产力提升有限，瓶颈在于软件开发的其他环节。
• LLM生成代码的质量和可靠性：部分评论认为LLM生成的代码质量高且附带额外提升，但也有评论指出其存在“幻觉”和不符合标准的问题。
• AI在不同任务上的表现差异：一些用户发现LLM在特定任务上表现优异，但在处理复杂问题时效果不佳。

总结：
评论主要围绕AI在软件开发中的实际生产力提升效果展开，争议焦点在于10x生产力提升的现实性、LLM生成代码的质量和可靠性以及AI在不同任务上的表现差异。多数评论认为AI能提升特定任务的效率，但对整体生产力的提升有限，瓶颈在于软件开发的其他环节。

44798189.article_content:
No, AI is not Making Engineers 10x as Productive
Curing Your AI 10x Engineer Imposter Syndrome
05 August 2025
AI
A few months ago I went through a bit of a mental slump. I've always been confident of my abilities as an engineer, but I couldn't help but feel like my skills were falling hopelessly behind as I scrolled places like LinkedIn and Twitter. If these sources were to be believed, engineering had moved on from the medieval practice of typing code into an editor.
Real
engineers were now 10-100x more productive than I was. I'm writing this hoping to help others who are feeling similar anxieties.
I'm a skeptical person so I don't usually fall over myself immediately when I hear a claim like that. I usually roll my eyes in the same way I do when someone tells me a simple herbal remedy cures all disease. But the sheer volume these 10x engineer claims are reaching right now started to hit a nerve. What if I'm
wrong
? Will I miss the bus and become unemployable if I don't learn to use AI right now? After all, there are a lot of fancy words going around that distance the "AI" these people are talking about with the "AI" I was familiar with.
These people were using
✨agentic✨
AI. They were using
✨thinking✨
models that surfed the internet, ran tests, and corrected their own mistakes. Sure I popped into a chat window here and there and asked it to write some code, then promptly discarded most of the output once I got the idea that I needed. But these engineers were letting Claude fully take the wheel and had agents ripping 5 PRs for them while they made morning coffee. Was I becoming a dinosaur, an old man yelling at cloud?
Part of what made me feel so anxious was that it was entirely possible AI changed without me knowing it because I didn't use AI very much. Because I didn't
like
using AI that much. Reviewing code is vastly less enjoyable process than writing it. Had my stubborn desire to
enjoy coding
set me up to be left behind?
Diving In
Eventually I hit a breaking point and decided I simply had to dive in head first to AI coding. I tried Claude Code, Cursor, Roo Code, and Zed for their agentic coding promises. I started asking AI to write all sorts of code in all sorts of projects. I tried the different models and compared them. I even vibe coded a few things, not editing the code manually once.
And it was... Fine. Despite claims that AI today is improving at a fever pitch, it felt largely the same as before. It's good at writing boilerplate, especially in Javascript, and particularly in React. It's not good at keeping up with the standards and utilities of your codebase. It tends to struggle with languages like Terraform. It still hallucinates libraries leading to significant
security vulnerabilities
.
AIs still struggle to absorb the context of a larger codebase, even with a great prompt and
CLAUDE.md
file. If you use a library that isn't StackOverflow's favorite it will butcher it even after an agentic lookup of the documentation. Agents occasionally do something neat like fix the tests they broke. Often they just waste time and tokens, going back and forth with themselves not seeming to gain any deeper knowledge each time they fail. Thus, AI's best use case for me remains writing one-off scripts. Especially when I have no interest in learning deeper fundamentals for a single script, like when writing a custom ESLint rule.
Dark warnings that if I didn't start using AI now I'd be hopelessly behind proved unfounded. Using AI to code is not hard to learn. Obviously? Well, the AI coding community seems split on whether AI makes coding so easy a caveman can do it and that it requires an advanced, dedicated prompt engineer skillset. There are a few things you need to learn but they come quickly. You learn how to split up tasks into smaller pieces so the AI doesn't lose its mind late in the context window. Tools like Claude Code can do a bit of this themselves, even, though not always reliably. And you learn to identify when the AI is too far off and it's time to take the wheel.
A competent engineer will figure this stuff out in less than a week of moderate AI usage. Further, if AI is about to get 2x, 10x, or 100x better at any minute (as everyone keeps saying it will), then any lessons about how to use it now are moot for the future.
Every time I encountered AI working "just okay", it strangely made me more anxious, not less. It meant I couldn't find the spicy secret sauce that made everyone else so productive. I just didn't have what it takes: dinosaur, meet asteroid, thy name is AI. Eventually, a few things shook me out of this slump. One of those was
this article
from Ludicity, directly countering the claims of the AI pumpers. I write this article to share more things that helped me get out of the AI 10x engineer imposter syndrome.
The Math
Let's start by looking at the simple math of 10-100x productivity. 10x productivity means ten times the outcomes, not ten times the lines of code. This means what you use

data.title: Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.0 with Debian 13 released
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: Proxmox Server Solutions发布了Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE) 9.0，该版本基于Debian 13 "Trixie"，采用Linux内核6.14.8-2，提升了硬件兼容性和性能。主要更新包括对厚配置LVM共享存储的快照支持，适用于iSCSI和FC SAN环境，并引入了SDN堆栈的"Fabrics"功能，支持复杂网络架构和自动故障转移。此外，高可用性（HA）集群增加了资源亲和性规则，优化资源分配，减少延迟。移动界面也经过重构，使用Rust框架Yew，提供更便捷的管理功能。该版本还更新了QEMU、LXC、Ceph和ZFS等开源技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Proxmox作为虚拟化平台在不同使用场景中的优缺点，以及与其他平台（如VMware、XCP-ng、LXD）的对比。

不同观点：
• **支持Proxmox的观点**：
  - [BLKNSLVR] 从ESXi转向了Proxmox，因为Proxmox在消费级硬件上的兼容性更好，尤其是网络设备的兼容性。他还提到Proxmox的备份过程非常可靠，VM恢复也很稳定。
  - [riedel] 他们在一个四台机器的集群中使用Proxmox，认为其功能对业余管理员和用户来说恰到好处。他们也赞赏Proxmox的论坛资源，但对扩展性和自定义集成的复杂性提出了一些批评。
  - [nativeit] 长期使用Proxmox，并对其最新版本表示赞赏。

• **对Proxmox的功能和可用性提出改进意见**：
  - [redundantly] 认为Proxmox缺乏像VMware的VMFS那样的共享存储功能，无法在多个节点之间实现VM的故障转移。
  - [avtar] 认为Proxmox在集群环境中表现良好，但在单节点上的VM和容器配置管理不如LXD/Incus方便，尤其是版本控制方面。
  - [BodyCulture] 指出Proxmox缺乏官方支持的磁盘加密功能，用户需要自行解决，可能导致一些问题。
  - [krisknez] 希望Proxmox能有一个用于端口转发的UI，而不必通过终端操作。

• **对Proxmox升级和兼容性的关注**：
  - [PeterStuer] 从Hyper-V转向Proxmox，关心Proxmox的升级过程是否顺利。
  - [grmone] 对Proxmox使用的Linux内核版本提出疑问，担心其是否自行 backport 安全补丁。
  - [throw0101c] 提供Proxmox VE 9.0的发布亮点链接，并提到XCP-ng作为一个替代选项，邀请使用过两者的人比较其优缺点。

• **关于Proxmox安装和UI技术的讨论**：
  - [Takennickname] 询问Proxmox是否一直可以安装在Debian上，回忆过去版本（如7.x）可能不支持此功能。
  - [xattt] 表示由于需要为集成Intel显卡实现SR-IOV功能，暂时不考虑转到Proxmox。
  - [yla92] 首次听说Yew框架（由Rust编写并编译为WASM的前端框架），并询问其他人是否有使用经验。

补充讨论：
- Proxmox的备份和恢复功能被广泛认可，尤其是在小型和业余环境中表现出色。
- 用户对Proxmox在扩展性和自定义集成方面的复杂性表示关注，尤其是与API和UI相关的自定义。
- 对Proxmox的磁盘加密和共享存储功能的需求被提及，显示出部分用户对安全性和高级功能的需求。
- 用户在考虑Proxmox时，对其升级过程的平滑程度和硬件兼容性表示关注。
- 提到了XCP-ng作为Proxmox的替代选项，引发了一些关于两者优缺点的讨论。

44798035.article_content:
Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.0 with Debian 13 released
August 05, 2025
Download:
English
German
VIENNA, Austria – August 05, 2025 –
Leading open-source server solutions provider Proxmox Server Solutions GmbH (henceforth "Proxmox"), celebrating its 20th year of innovation, today announced the release of Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE) 9.0. Main highlight of this update is a modernized core built upon Debian 13 “Trixie”, ensuring a robust foundation for the platform.
Proxmox VE 9.0 further introduces significant advancements in both storage and networking capabilities, addressing critical enterprise demands. A highlight is the long-awaited support for snapshots on thick-provisioned LVM shared storage, improving storage management capabilities especially for enterprise users with Fibre Channel (FC) or iSCSI SAN environments. With newly added “fabric” support for Software-Defined Networking (SDN), administrators can construct highly complex and scalable network architectures.
Highlights in Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.0
Debian 13 “Trixie” at the core
This core update is based on Debian 13 “Trixie”, bringing the latest Debian release as foundation for Proxmox VE including newer packages, improved hardware support, and enhanced security. Proxmox VE is using a newer Linux kernel 6.14.8-2 as stable default enhancing hardware compatibility and performance.
Also, updates to the latest versions of leading open-source technologies for virtual environments like QEMU 10.0.2, LXC 6.0.4, Ceph Squid 19.2.3, and ZFS 2.3.3 are included. ZFS now supports adding new devices to existing RAIDZ pools with minimal downtime. For existing users of Proxmox VE 8.4 or older versions, an extensively tested and detailed upgrade path is available to enable a smooth upgrade.
Snapshots for thick-provisioned LVM shared storage
Virtual Machines (VMs) utilizing thick-provisioned LVM shared storages, such as those backed by iSCSI or FC-based SANs, now benefit from snapshot functionality out of the box. This is achieved by implementing snapshots as volume chains, where a volume based on a snapshot only records differences to its parent snapshot volume. Directory, NFS, and CIFS storages also gain additional support for snapshots as volume chains.
This new feature provides a powerful and highly requested capability for customers with traditional SAN infrastructure who have historically relied on clustered file systems. While direct integrations from many storage vendors continue to grow, this new feature closes the gap by providing a storage-independent solution for snapshots. This gives customers the independence to seamlessly manage their snapshots regardless of their hardware, without compromising on convenience.
New Fabrics feature for the SDN stack
This release enhances the SDN capabilities with the introduction of an SDN Fabrics feature, designed to simplify the configuration and management of complex routed networks. Engineered for reliability, SDN Fabrics facilitates multiple paths between nodes and automatic failover across Network Interface Cards (NICs), enabling the configuration of robust two-layer spine-leaf architectures for improved network redundancy and performance.
This new feature simplifies the management of dynamically routed networks which can for example be used as Ethernet VPN (EVPN) underlay or full-mesh networks for Ceph. The SDN stack in Proxmox VE gains support for two different routing protocols, OpenFabric and OSPF, and provides intuitive tools for the simplified configuration and precise management of those dynamic routing protocols.
Affinity rules in High Availability (HA) clusters
The Proxmox team introduces HA resource affinity rules to enable fine-grained control and flexibility over resource placement in HA clusters, ensuring optimal performance, enhanced resiliency, and minimized latency for critical workloads. To better control complex, interconnected applications, the new HA Resource Affinity Rules allow administrators to precisely define how virtual machines and other HA resources are distributed across a cluster.
Interdependent HA resources, such as for example an application server and its associated database, can be kept together on the same physical node to minimize network latency. For services requiring maximum redundancy, like multiple VMs running the same mission-critical application, the rules can ensure these instances are kept on different nodes. This increases fault tolerance and ensures resiliency even during HA failovers.
Enhanced mobile interface
The Proxmox VE mobile interface has been thoroughly reworked, using the new Proxmox widget toolkit powered by the Rust-based Yew framework. The redesigned interface provides quick access to service overviews and includes essential management functions, including starting and stopping virtual guests and basic configuration. It is now easier than ever for users to access fundamental functionalities of Proxmox VE directly from their mobile browsers.

data.title: TSMC says employees tried to steal trade secrets on iPhone 18 chip process
data.author: mikece
data.article_summary: 台积电（TSMC）指控数名前员工试图窃取与其2纳米芯片工艺相关的商业机密，这些工艺预计将用于明年iPhone 18系列的A20芯片。台积电发现这些员工存在未经授权的活动后，已解雇并对他们提起法律诉讼，这些前员工可能还将面临刑事起诉。台积电强调，他们在例行监控中发现异常访问模式，从而揭露了潜在的商业机密泄露。台湾检方已确认介入调查，并表示将依法严惩。尽管未透露具体被盗信息，但此事可能涉及更广泛的2纳米工艺技术，而非仅限于苹果的A20芯片。这一事件甚至可能涉及国家安全问题，因为台湾政府对保护国内先进技术极为重视。

TSMC says employees tried to steal trade secrets on iPhone 18 chip process
Ben Lovejoy
| Aug 5 2025 - 5:19 am PT
0 Comments
Apple
chipmaker
TSMC
has said that several then-employees tried to steal trade secrets relating to the company’s most advanced chip process. TSMC fired the individuals concerned and is now taking legal action against them. The former employees may also face criminal prosecution.
The report relates to the company’s 2-nanometer chip process, which is expected to be used for the A20 chips across next year’s
iPhone 18
lineup …
TSMC 2nm process expected to debut in iPhone 18
TSMC leads the world in the most advanced chip processes, and is next year expected to use its 2nm technology
for the A20 chips
used in the iPhone 18 range. Apple typically gets access to TSMC’s most advanced chip processes ahead of the company’s other customers.
Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has suggested that the new chip will be
used for all iPhone 18 models
, not just the two Pro ones.
TSMC says employees tried to steal trade secrets
Nikkei Asia
reports that TSMC accused several former employees of attempting to obtain secret information about its 2nm chip development and production process.
Several former employees of TSMC are suspected of attempting to obtain critical proprietary information on 2-nanometer chip development and production while working at the company, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.
In response to Nikkei Asia’s questions, TSMC said that it recently “detected unauthorized activities during routine monitoring, leading to the discovery of potential trade secret leaks.”
The world’s top chipmaker said on Monday it took “strict disciplinary actions against the personnel involved and has initiated legal proceedings.”
The attempt was detected by spotting “unusual access patterns” on the part of one of the employees.
The report says there could even be national security implications, as the Taiwanese government takes extremely seriously the protection of advanced technology developed within the country. Prosecutors have confirmed that they are investigating, and TSMC says that it will seek prosecution to the fullest extent of the law.
No details have been shared on the nature of the information obtained. It is likely that it relates to the 2nm process in general rather than anything specific to Apple’s A20 chip.

data.author: prodbro
data.article_summary: SimpleW是一个基于.NET Core的web服务器库，主打功能强大且简洁快速。它支持多种功能，包括路由、REST API（自动JSON序列化/反序列化）、Json Web Token、WebSocket、Server Sent Events、静态文件服务和OpenTelemetry等。该库遵循MIT许可证，文档可在官方网站查看，更新日志详细记录了每个版本的变化。用户可以提交问题报告，参与贡献。当前，SimpleW在GitHub上有41颗星和5个分支，具有较高的开发活跃度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕NetCoreServer及相关技术（如Kestrel、IIS）在生产环境中的适用性和性能比较

不同观点：
• bob1029认为NetCoreServer虽然不错，但相比Kestrel或IIS，他不愿意在生产环境中使用。他认为Kestrel在性能上很难被超越，并且不喜欢ASP.NET Core自带的复杂功能，更倾向于使用最小化的API和轻量级的HttpContext处理程序。

• andix对bob1029的观点提出质疑，认为ASP.NET Core是非常优秀的web框架，具有极高的模块化和灵活性，其底层组件（如HTTP服务器、路由）可以作为新web框架的基础。

• anditherobot关心是否可以不再安装Nginx或IIS，暗示对简化服务器设置的需求或疑问。

• mrweasel支持NetCoreServer的简单性，提到Kestrel的配置和运行让他感到困惑，认为NetCoreServer看起来更简单。

补充讨论：
• aanthonymax的评论提到VitePress的文档看起来不错，但与主要讨论的技术话题无直接关联，属于题外话。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于NetCoreServer与Kestrel、IIS在生产环境中的适用性和性能比较。具体来说，bob1029和andix在ASP.NET Core框架的复杂性和必要性上存在分歧，而mrweasel则关注于技术的易用性。

data.title: The Age of Bronze and Steel
data.author: panic
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了3D打印金属工艺的终结及其背后的商业故事。一种名为“粘结剂喷射钢加青铜渗透”的独特3D打印工艺因市场和公司收购问题而消失。2021年，Desktop Metal收购了该技术的发明公司ExOne，并提高价格，但未能成功建立可持续的商业模式。尽管通过法律手段迫使Nano Dimensions完成收购，Desktop Metal最终仍申请破产。该工艺因依赖于有经验的工程师操作，且这些工程师退休或离职，导致技术失传。文章还将此情况与游戏行业的Embracer Group进行对比，指出技术及行业的脆弱性，强调了某些技术可能突然消失的风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：材料在光学实验室仪器夹具中的应用及其可行性

不同观点：
• **[不支持使用该材料]**：s0rce基于十年前作为博士后研究员的经验指出，这种材料的尺寸公差较差，无法直接使用，需要进一步加工到最终尺寸。相比之下，直接用铝加工或树脂打印更合理。这表明该材料在精密光学仪器中应用有局限性。
   
• **[支持传统材料]**：从成本和效率的角度来看，s0rce认为使用铝或树脂打印更符合实际需求，因为这些材料或方法不需要额外的加工，减少了工作量和潜在的误差。

补充讨论：
• **[技术进步的可能性]**：尽管s0rce十年前的经验指出该材料有公差问题，但评论中未提及该材料是否有技术改进。随着时间的推移，材料科学可能已经解决了部分公差和加工问题，因此未来可能会有不同的结论。

• **[具体应用场景的影响]**：该评论暗示，材料的选择可能与具体应用场景有关。在光学实验室中，对尺寸精度的要求非常高，因此对材料的公差要求也更严格。这表明在其他要求不那么严格的场景中，该材料可能仍然有应用潜力。

• **[争议焦点]**：该材料的公差问题是否已经通过技术改进得到解决，或者是否存在新的加工技术能够弥补这些缺陷，是争议的核心。这需要更多的实验或实际应用来验证。
