• 评论中涉及了PNG的各种优化方案和替代格式，如JPEG XL、FPNG、ZPNG、QOI等，讨论了它们的压缩速度、文件大小、兼容性和硬件要求等。

One of the issues we have with .PNG is slow read/write times. There are now new lossless open source codecs without patent concerns, such as Zstandard (maintained by Facebook) or LZ4:
https://facebook.github.io/zstd/
https://github.com/lz4/lz4
Zstandard is used by the new Khronos KTX2 GPU texture format specification. I propose that it be added as an option to a future version of .PNG. The possible speedups are quite significant, and for users that read and write a lot of .PNG's as part of their data processing pipelines the speedups will be high value improvements.
There are also other far simpler but even faster codecs being developed, such as .QOI's, but using this would likely require changing or not filtering the image before compression:
https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=29328750

data.author: lackoftactics

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源模型与技术进展的比较和未来发展

不同观点：
• **foundry27**：从技术角度分析了新发布模型的架构，认为该模型在技术上并没有显著的创新。例如，与Deepseek、Qwen、GLM和Kimi等领先的开源模型相比，新模型在多头注意力机制和专家混合架构上没有采用一些最新的改进。不过，该模型在量化解决方案上有亮点，能够在80GB的GPU上运行120B的模型，但总体上保持了技术优势未公开。

• **ClassAndBurn**：认为开源模型将在长期竞争中胜出，因为开放模型可以加速创新并降低开发成本。提到中国企业快速迭代开源模型的例子，并预测美国基础模型制造商可能会在未来1-3次迭代中开源前一代模型。此外，认为开源模型可以带来更多专门化和定制化的应用场景，最终推动科技和工程领域的发展。

• **x187463**：对能够在24GB的Mac Mini上运行与o3相当的模型表示惊讶，认为这种进展速度非常快，并预期未来能够在移动设备上运行类似模型。

• **deviation**：推测新模型的发布可能预示着即将发布更强大的模型，并从战略角度分析发布时机。

• **timmg**：赞赏Ollama的易用性，强调其快速发现和使用新模型的便利。

• **artembugara**：询问运行20个并发进程所需的资源，以及与gpt-4.1-nano相比的性能和自托管成本。

• **henriquegodoy**：对20B模型能在如此小的规模下实现高性能表示兴奋，认为这将改变软件开发方式，特别是在本地运行高性能模型的情况下。

• **sadiq**：提到Groq和Fireworks已经在openrouter上运行，并给出相关的成本数据。

• **IceHegel**：对新模型在基准测试中只比o3低约5分的性能表示印象深刻，并猜测是否因为GPT-5的即将发布使得公司更愿意发布当前模型。

• **user_7832**：提出新手问题，询问Kimi 2的发布是否可能导致OpenAI推迟其模型的发布。

• **mythz**：分享了在多张GPU上运行gpt-oss模型的性能数据，发现不同硬件配置下性能差异显著。

• **thimabi**：对OpenAI开源性能与o3和o4-mini相当的模型表示惊讶，并询问是否有潜在的“陷阱”。

• **jakozaur**：认为编码是LLM的强项，但当前模型消耗太多 tokens，提出混合架构的解决方案，让本地模型处理简单任务，而更强模型处理复杂任务。

• **HanClinto**：提到已经有llama.cpp的支持，并给出相关链接。

• **Leary**：提供了新模型在不同基准测试中的得分，与其他模型进行对比。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是新模型是否真的具备技术创新，foundry27认为创新有限，而其他人如henriquegodoy则对其高性能和小型化表示兴奋。
• 另一个讨论点是开源模型的长期价值与商业模型的竞争，ClassAndBurn强调开源模型能加速创新并降低成本。
• 技术细节如量化解决方案、运行所需的硬件资源、以及混合架构的应用也在讨论中被频繁提及。

data.article_summary: 2025年8月5日，Anthropic发布了Claude Opus 4.1，这是对Claude Opus 4的升级，特别在代理任务、实际编码和推理能力方面有显著提升。Opus 4.1在SWE-bench Verified上的编码性能达到74.5%，并在多文件代码重构、数据分析和细节追踪上表现更佳。多家公司如Rakuten Group和Windsurf均反馈4.1版本在调试和开发任务中表现优异。该版本现已对付费用户和通过API等平台提供，价格与Opus 4相同。建议所有用户升级至Opus 4.1，并欢迎反馈以帮助进一步改进模型。

44800185.article_content:
Announcements
Claude Opus 4.1
Aug 5, 2025
●
1 min
read
Today we're releasing Claude Opus 4.1, an upgrade to Claude Opus 4 on agentic tasks, real-world coding, and reasoning. We plan to release substantially larger improvements to our models in the coming weeks.
Opus 4.1 is now available to paid Claude users and in Claude Code. It's also on our API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud's Vertex AI. Pricing is the same as Opus 4.
Claude Opus 4.1
Opus 4.1 advances our state-of-the-art coding performance to 74.5% on
SWE-bench Verified
. It also improves Claude’s in-depth research and data analysis skills, especially around detail tracking and agentic search.
GitHub
notes that Claude Opus 4.1 improves across most capabilities relative to Opus 4, with particularly notable performance gains in multi-file code refactoring.
Rakuten Group
finds that Opus 4.1 excels at pinpointing exact corrections within large codebases without making unnecessary adjustments or introducing bugs, with their team preferring this precision for everyday debugging tasks.
Windsurf
reports Opus 4.1 delivers a one standard deviation improvement over Opus 4 on their junior developer benchmark, showing roughly the same performance leap as the jump from Sonnet 3.7 to Sonnet 4.
Getting started
We recommend upgrading from Opus 4 to Opus 4.1 for all uses. If you’re a developer, simply use
claude-opus-4-1-20250805
via the API. You can also explore our
system card
,
model page
,
pricing page
, and
docs
to learn more.
As always, your
feedback
helps us improve, especially as we continue to release new and more capable models.
Appendix
Data sources
OpenAI:
o3 launch post
,
o3 system card
Gemini:
2.5 Pro model card
Claude:
Sonnet 3.7 launch post
,
Claude 4 launch post
Benchmark reporting
Claude models are hybrid reasoning models. The benchmarks reported in this blog post show the highest scores achieved with or without extended thinking. We’ve noted below for each result whether extended thinking was used:
No extended thinking: SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench
The following benchmarks were reported with extended thinking (up to 64K tokens): TAU-bench, GPQA Diamond, MMMLU, MMMU, AIME
TAU-bench methodology
Scores were achieved with a prompt addendum to both the Airline and Retail Agent Policy instructing Claude to better leverage its reasoning abilities while using extended thinking with tool use. The model is encouraged to write down its thoughts as it solves the problem distinct from our usual thinking mode, during the multi-turn trajectories to best leverage its reasoning abilities. To accommodate the additional steps Claude incurs by utilizing more thinking, the maximum number of steps (counted by model completions) was increased from 30 to 100 (most trajectories completed under 30 steps with only one trajectory reaching above 50 steps).
SWE-bench methodology
For the Claude 4 family of models, we continue to use the same simple scaffold that equips the model with solely the two tools described in our prior releases
here
—a bash tool, and a file editing tool that operates via string replacements. We no longer include the
third ‘planning tool’
used by Claude 3.7 Sonnet. On all Claude 4 models, we report scores out of the full 500 problems. Scores for OpenAI models are reported out of a
477 problem subset
.

• [minimaxir] 指出尽管Opus有改进，但如果成本不变，Sonnet的性价比仍然更高。根据OpenRouter的数据，Sonnet生成的tokens数量远多于Opus。

补充讨论：
• [qsort] 提到三大实验室几乎同时发布了新模型，认为这是一个疯狂的动漫情节。

The current US administration, led by President Donald Trump, has employed trade tariffs as the primary way to reduce the US's trade deficit with partner countries. However, the US tariff policy has been erratic and unpredictable. These tariffs have also affected Taiwan, one of the US’s biggest trading partners.
Currently standing at 20%, the US trade tariff on Taiwan is more than that of countries like Japan, which pays a baseline tariff of 15%. Unsurprisingly, a 20% levy on Taiwanese exports to the US will hurt Taiwanese businesses quite a bit, which is why the country needs to negotiate further with the US to bring the tariffs down or downright eliminate then. However, according to a new report out of Taiwan, US President Trump has presented Taiwan with two conditions for tariff relief, both of which are quite stringent.
Per the Taiwanese outlet mnews.tw
, an industry source told the publication that President Donald Trump has mandated TSMC fulfill two conditions if Taiwan is to see any tariff reduction:
Buy a 49% stake in Intel
Invest a further $400 billion in the US
While ignoring the industrial ramifications of TSMC owning 49% of Intel, these are humongous financial commitments.
TSMC is already investing a ton of money in the US
, with one of the company’s fabs achieving volume production in 2024. The Taiwanese giant is on its way to building two more fabs at its Arizona facility, alongside an R&D Center and a packaging facility. Overall, TSMC has planned to invest a total of $165 billion in the US.
So, President Trump’s alleged condition of investing a further $400 billion in the US alongside buying a stake in Intel seems improbable from a purely financial standpoint.
The US is trying to save Intel from collapse
Intel is on the decline
. From the
company’s fab operations
to consumer products, virtually every Intel department is taking a hit. This has shown in the company’s reported annual revenue figure, which has come down from a high of $79 billion in 2021 to $53 billion in 2024, is a massive 33% reduction.
Intel is a vital part of the US’s plans regarding domestic semiconductor manufacturing. As such,
the company has already received billions in federal grants
. However, this funding has not solved Intel’s troubles, as the company has delayed its Ohio fab from an initial target of 2025 to 2030/31. A primary reason for this delay seems to be Intel’s efforts to preserve capital resources amidst a lack of significant help from the US CHIPS Act and outside partners.
In short, the US administration seems to be pressuring TSMC to acquire a considerable stake in Intel to inject some much-needed capital into the company and keep the US government's plans of a domestic chip supply chain afloat. However, TSMC is unlikely to agree to this proposal.
It'd be interesting to see what happens to Intel the coming months. Intel has a few exciting products in the works with
Panther Lake
and
Nova Lake CPUs
. So, things could improve for Team Blue if these products deliver.

data.title: Show HN: Whittle – A shrinking word game
data.author: babel16
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一款字谜游戏的反馈，包括游戏机制、用户界面（UI）、技术问题和总体体验。

不同观点：
• **关于游戏机制和目标的困惑**：
  - [jsnell] 认为有两个目标（消除所有字母和找到所有单词）让人困惑，尤其是因为游戏通过颜色提示推动玩家去找到所有单词，而这让人感觉乏味。
  - [teach] 和 [spadros] 质疑是否总能将字母减少到单个字母，并希望有提示功能来帮助完成 puzzle。
  - [yobananaboy] 建议当减少到一个字母时触发胜利状态，而不是必须到0。

• **技术问题和错误报告**：
  - [davidsojevic] 和 [hackyhacky] 都提到在不同浏览器中遇到的技术问题，特别是 "puzzleLog" 错误，导致无法开始游戏。
  - [fao_] 提到分享按钮在PC上无法工作。

• **用户界面和用户体验反馈**：
  - [jsnell] 认为桌面版的UI缺少悬停效果，尤其是字母点击时没有变化或光标样式，影响了操作体验。
  - [pimlottc] 提到初始状态不明确，不知道字母可以直接点击，且底部未标记的标签令人困惑。此外，帮助界面上的点让人误以为是移动端的滑动操作。
  - 相反，[jessecoleman] 赞扬了UX设计，认为其很优秀。

• **游戏灵感与对比**：
  - [c22] 提到该游戏与自己曾经玩过的类似游戏有相似之处，都是通过字母操作。
  - [onion92] 指出他们的想法与另一个网站相似，并分享了链接。

• **其他建议和调侃**：
  - [jangerhofer] 提醒玩家空格也是可操作字符，解决了部分玩家初次游戏时的困惑。
  - [spadros] 请求添加提示功能以帮助完成挑战。
  - [werds] 调侃游戏可能会被纽约时报收购，类似于Wordle的命运。

补充讨论：
- 游戏的胜利状态不明确，[duncancarroll] 提到完成后没有明显的胜利提示，让人困惑。
- 游戏的目标和策略存在争议，[jsnell] 认为从可能的1/2字母单词反推是主要策略，但未测试字典的合理性。

争议的焦点：
- 游戏有两个目标是否必要，尤其是找到所有单词的目标被部分玩家认为乏味且不明确。
- 技术问题特别是浏览器兼容性和错误报告，影响了部分玩家的游戏体验。

主要讨论点：关于内容中提及的128k上下文长度以及"OSS"的含义的讨论

不同观点：
• tonyhart7 对于128k上下文长度表示疑问，似乎认为这个长度较短，可能期待更大的上下文长度。此评论虽然没有直接提出反对意见，但通过反问表达了对当前限制的不满或惊讶。

• alexshendi 对"OSS"的含义提出了幽默的猜测，将其与"Office of Strategic Services"（战略服务办公室）联系起来，而不是通常在技术讨论中指代的"开放源代码软件"（Open Source Software）。这一评论带有调侃性质，暗示对缩写的不同理解可能导致混淆。

补充讨论：
- tonyhart7 的评论反映了部分技术社区对模型性能参数（如上下文长度）的高期望，尤其是在处理复杂任务或大数据集时。
- alexshendi 的评论提醒了在技术讨论中使用缩写的潜在歧义，强调了在交流中明确表达的重要性，尤其是在跨领域的讨论中。

这两个评论代表了在技术讨论中常见的两种情况：对技术规格的关注和期待，以及对术语和缩写的澄清需求。

data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: GitHub提供事件通知服务，用户可通过电子邮件或短信接收事故创建、更新、解决的通知。用户需输入电子邮箱或电话号码，并验证OTP以订阅通知。通知范围包括事件更新和组件状态变化，也支持通过Slack或webhook接收通知。此外，GitHub还通报了一起已解决的拉取请求事故，并承诺分享根本原因分析。订阅需同意隐私政策和服务条款。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub的功能膨胀及其带来的核心功能问题，以及用户对该平台的信任和使用方式的讨论。

不同观点：
• [keb_] 认为GitHub的功能膨胀导致核心功能（如PR审查）出现问题，尤其是处理大型PR时性能不佳。
• [lrvick] 和 [john01dav] 支持使用自我托管的解决方案（如Forgejo和gitea），强调Git的去中心化特性，并对托管解决方案表示不信任。
• [bdcravens] 提到Hacker News（HN）社区的变化，指出以前会有更多关于安装GitLab的讨论，而现在这种声音少了。
• [njovin] 赞扬GitHub的状态页面准确，认为相比AWS和Google，GitHub在这方面做得更好。

补充讨论：
• [dang] 提供了一个相关讨论链接，涉及GitHub UI变慢的问题，表明该问题已经引起过社区关注。
• [rileymichael] 引用商业新闻，质疑GitHub的开发团队是否发生了变动，暗示可能与平台问题有关。
• [arccy] 以讽刺的语气评论，似乎认为GitHub的代码审查存在问题，可能与自动代码审查工具Copilot有关。
• [pelagicAustral] 和 [antihero] 以幽默的方式回应，前者表示自己直接在主分支上提交代码，后者则开玩笑说应该拥抱AI。
• [clysm] 质疑为什么问题通过PR而不是状态页面来解决，表明对GitHub处理方式的不满。
• [politelemon] 提出一个悖论式的问题，询问GitHub的开发是否发生在GitHub上，如果PR系统出问题，他们如何审查修复PR的PR。
• [ItsABytecode] 以幽默回应，暗示自己刚合并的代码可能导致了问题。
• [axelpacheco] 则尝试量化GitHub PR问题导致的每小时经济损失，强调问题的重要性。

争议焦点：GitHub功能膨胀是否导致核心功能问题，以及用户对托管解决方案的不信任与自我托管方案的对比。

data.title: Ozempic shows anti-aging effects in trial
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 一项随机对照试验对108名患有HIV相关脂肪代谢障碍的患者进行了研究，发现每周使用Ozempic（司美鲁肽）治疗32周后，受试者的生物学年龄平均逆转了3.1年。研究使用表观遗传时钟测量生物学衰老，发现最显著的抗衰老效果体现在炎症系统和大脑，衰老被延迟了近5年。研究人员认为，司美鲁肽通过改善脂肪分布和减少炎症，从而减缓细胞衰老。尽管结果令人鼓舞，但研究者 caution 不要过早将Ozempic广泛用于抗衰老治疗，但指出该药物在抗衰老领域的潜力巨大。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• Pitpatagain指出，该研究仅针对HIV相关脂肪代谢障碍的人群，其结果未必适用于普通人群。

• Charlie0和jsbg质疑，Ozempic的抗衰老效果是否仅仅源于体重减轻本身，而非药物的特定效果。
• Getpost引用Ben Bikman的播客，讨论GLP-1药物的历史和潜在风险，指出早期小剂量使用可能更安全。
• Neves警告不要轻信“奇迹药物”的宣传，分享其母亲因服用Ozempic出现严重副作用的个人经历，强调长期效果仍不明确。
• Lysecret对semaglutides的更多积极效果表示兴奋。

• V__对使用表观遗传时钟的研究持怀疑态度，认为这些研究的结果误差较大，不可靠。
• Thurn关注semaglutides的价格问题，询问是否有可能在印度等国家获得价格更低的仿制药。

• Heraldgeezer提倡通过禁食而非药物来达到健康效果。

• 争议的焦点在于semaglutides的实际效果和安全性，尤其是长期使用的未知风险。

• 个人经历（如neves的母亲）为讨论增加了对药物副作用的实际担忧。
• 价格和获取途径也是讨论的重要部分，特别是在低成本仿制药的可行性上。

44798410.article_content:
Key Insights
A randomized controlled trial of 108 people with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy found that weekly Ozempic treatment for 32 weeks reversed biological age by an average of 3.1 years.
The study used epigenetic clocks to measure biological aging, showing the most pronounced anti-aging effects in the inflammatory system and brain, where aging was delayed by almost 5 years.
Researchers believe the anti-aging effects stem from semaglutide's ability to improve fat distribution and reduce inflammation, both major drivers of cellular aging.
The diabetes drug Ozempic has demonstrated remarkable anti-aging effects in the first clinical trial to directly measure its impact on biological aging, with participants becoming an average of 3.1 years biologically younger after 32 weeks of treatment. The findings provide the strongest evidence yet that GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide may offer benefits far beyond their established roles in diabetes management and weight loss.
First Direct Clinical Evidence of Anti-Aging Effects
Varun Dwaraka from diagnostics company TruDiagnostic in Lexington, Kentucky, led a randomized controlled trial involving 108 people with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy, a condition characterized by excess fat accumulation and accelerated cellular aging. Half the participants received weekly Ozempic injections for 32 weeks, while the other half received a placebo.
The researchers used epigenetic clocks to assess biological aging - sophisticated tools that identify patterns of DNA methylation, chemical tags that affect gene activity and shift predictably with age. These patterns can be accelerated or slowed by lifestyle factors, meaning biological age can differ significantly from chronological age.
"Those on semaglutide became, on average, 3.1 years biologically younger by the end of the study," Dwaraka reported. The placebo group showed no significant change in biological age over the same period.
Organ-Specific Anti-Aging Benefits
The anti-aging effects weren't uniform across all body systems. The research team found that semaglutide slowed biological aging in several organs and systems, with the most dramatic improvements occurring in the inflammatory system and brain, where the drug appeared to delay biological aging by almost 5 years. Significant benefits were also observed in the heart and kidneys.
"Semaglutide may not only slow the rate of ageing, but in some individuals partially reverse it," Dwaraka noted, highlighting the potential for the drug to actually turn back the biological clock rather than simply slowing its progression.
Mechanisms Behind the Anti-Aging Effects
The researchers believe semaglutide's anti-aging properties stem from its effects on fat distribution and metabolic health. Excess fat around organs triggers the release of pro-aging molecules that alter DNA methylation in key aging-related genes. By reducing this harmful fat accumulation and preventing low-grade inflammation - both major drivers of epigenetic aging - semaglutide appears to create a more youthful biological environment.
Randy Seeley from the University of Michigan Medical School expressed little surprise at the findings, explaining that the drugs "reduce the metabolic burden on a wide range of cells and lower inflammation. Both are major drivers of ageing in many different types of cells." However, he believes much of the benefit stems not from semaglutide's direct cellular effects, but from broader improvements to overall health.
Broader Implications and Future Directions
While the study focused specifically on people with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy, the biological pathways affected by semaglutide aren't unique to this condition. "Therefore, it is plausible that similar effects on epigenetic ageing could be observed in other populations," Dwaraka explained, suggesting the anti-aging benefits could extend to the general population.
Despite the promising results, Dwaraka cautioned against rushing to prescribe semaglutide broadly as an anti-aging therapy. "Prescribing it more broadly as an anti-ageing therapy is premature," he stated. However, he noted that the study adds momentum to ongoing efforts to repurpose existing drugs for age-related problems, which could speed approval processes and reduce the risk of unexpected side effects.
The research represents a significant milestone in understanding the full therapeutic potential of GLP-1 drugs, which have already gained prominence for treating type 2 diabetes and obesity, and are being explored for cardiovascular disease, addiction, and dementia. "Semaglutide may well emerge as one of the most promising candidates in this space," Dwaraka concluded.

data.title: Eleven Music
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: ElevenLabs推出了Eleven Music，一个通过自然语言提示生成高品质音乐的平台。用户可以控制音乐的流派、风格、结构，选择带人声或纯音乐，支持多种语言。该平台允许编辑歌曲的个别部分或整个歌曲的声音和歌词，且音乐可用于影视、播客、广告、游戏等多种商业用途。平台提供了多个示例歌曲，如《Echoes of Midnight》和《Saddles and Shadows》。Eleven Music现已在官网推出，并将很快提供公共API访问和与对话式AI平台的集成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容（尤其是音乐）的现状与未来影响

不同观点：
• **AI生成音乐缺乏艺术性与创新**：[two-sandwich] 认为AI生成的音乐缺乏对边界的突破和创新的探索，仅仅是为了满足观众的预期，属于纯粹的娱乐而非艺术。这种音乐没有灵魂和生命力，令人感到反乌托邦。
• **期待更具协作性与迭代性的AI工具**：[stillpointlab] 希望AI模型能够更加协作与迭代，而非像目前的“吃角子机”式生成工具。他设想一个能与艺术家互动的模型，帮助填补创作中的空白，例如为歌曲自动添加鼓点。
• **AI可能引发“有机”人类文化的复兴**：[sys32768] 认为AI将促使人们更加珍惜真人演奏的音乐和艺术，同时淘汰掉一些平庸的艺术家和音乐人。
• **AI在音乐分析中的潜在应用**：[abdullahkhalids] 提出AI是否能用于分析音乐中的和弦和音符，这表明AI在音乐学习与教育中的潜在用途。
• **AI生成音乐的商业与娱乐用途**：[amradio1989] 认为AI生成的音乐主要适用于那些音乐不占重要地位的场景，例如播客或营销活动，而非专业音乐制作。
• **对AI替代人类艺术家的担忧**：[throwaway1280] 作为音乐人，表达了对AI可能取代真人艺术家的担忧，认为AI生成音乐让音乐创作变得毫无意义。
• **AI生成音乐缺乏灵魂与意图**：[thepryz] 认为AI生成的音乐缺乏艺术的灵魂和创作意图，担心音乐会因此变得肤浅。
• **AI工具的营销语言问题**：[fidotron] 指出AI工具不仅输出内容令人不安，而且使用者还必须用企业化的语言来描述需求，这使得整个过程更加令人不适。

补充讨论：
• **AI生成音乐的技术成就与潜在用途**：[bigfishrunning] 和 [yanis_t] 对AI生成音乐的技术表示赞赏，但同时也表达了对这种技术带来的潜在负面影响的担忧。[pr337h4m] 提出AI可以在音乐风格搜索中发挥作用，类似于图像搜索的应用。
• **对AI生成艺术的极端反感**：[throwawayoldie] 对使用AI生成艺术的行为表示强烈反感，甚至用激烈的语言表达不满。
• **对未来AI主导文化的悲观预测**：[feoren] 认为当前的趋势是从我们曾经幻想的机器人解放人类的乌托邦走向了一个令人沮丧的反乌托邦，机器人正在侵占人类的创造性工作。

争议焦点：
• **AI生成音乐是否属于艺术**：一部分人认为AI生成音乐缺乏艺术性，而另一部分人则认为它可以在某些场景下发挥作用。
• **AI对音乐创作的影响是积极还是消极**：有些人认为AI会带来“有机”文化的复兴，而另一些人则担心AI会取代真人艺术家，使得创作变得肤浅和无意义。

44799479.article_summary: ElevenLabs推出了Eleven Music，一个通过自然语言提示生成高品质音乐的平台。用户可以控制音乐的流派、风格、结构，选择带人声或纯音乐，支持多种语言。该平台允许编辑歌曲的个别部分或整个歌曲的声音和歌词，且音乐可用于影视、播客、广告、游戏等多种商业用途。平台提供了多个示例歌曲，如《Echoes of Midnight》和《Saddles and Shadows》。Eleven Music现已在官网推出，并将很快提供公共API访问和与对话式AI平台的集成。
44799479.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容（尤其是音乐）的现状与未来影响

不同观点：
• **AI生成音乐缺乏艺术性与创新**：[two-sandwich] 认为AI生成的音乐缺乏对边界的突破和创新的探索，仅仅是为了满足观众的预期，属于纯粹的娱乐而非艺术。这种音乐没有灵魂和生命力，令人感到反乌托邦。
• **期待更具协作性与迭代性的AI工具**：[stillpointlab] 希望AI模型能够更加协作与迭代，而非像目前的“吃角子机”式生成工具。他设想一个能与艺术家互动的模型，帮助填补创作中的空白，例如为歌曲自动添加鼓点。
• **AI可能引发“有机”人类文化的复兴**：[sys32768] 认为AI将促使人们更加珍惜真人演奏的音乐和艺术，同时淘汰掉一些平庸的艺术家和音乐人。
• **AI在音乐分析中的潜在应用**：[abdullahkhalids] 提出AI是否能用于分析音乐中的和弦和音符，这表明AI在音乐学习与教育中的潜在用途。
• **AI生成音乐的商业与娱乐用途**：[amradio1989] 认为AI生成的音乐主要适用于那些音乐不占重要地位的场景，例如播客或营销活动，而非专业音乐制作。
• **对AI替代人类艺术家的担忧**：[throwaway1280] 作为音乐人，表达了对AI可能取代真人艺术家的担忧，认为AI生成音乐让音乐创作变得毫无意义。
• **AI生成音乐缺乏灵魂与意图**：[thepryz] 认为AI生成的音乐缺乏艺术的灵魂和创作意图，担心音乐会因此变得肤浅。
• **AI工具的营销语言问题**：[fidotron] 指出AI工具不仅输出内容令人不安，而且使用者还必须用企业化的语言来描述需求，这使得整个过程更加令人不适。

补充讨论：
• **AI生成音乐的技术成就与潜在用途**：[bigfishrunning] 和 [yanis_t] 对AI生成音乐的技术表示赞赏，但同时也表达了对这种技术带来的潜在负面影响的担忧。[pr337h4m] 提出AI可以在音乐风格搜索中发挥作用，类似于图像搜索的应用。
• **对AI生成艺术的极端反感**：[throwawayoldie] 对使用AI生成艺术的行为表示强烈反感，甚至用激烈的语言表达不满。
• **对未来AI主导文化的悲观预测**：[feoren] 认为当前的趋势是从我们曾经幻想的机器人解放人类的乌托邦走向了一个令人沮丧的反乌托邦，机器人正在侵占人类的创造性工作。

争议焦点：
• **AI生成音乐是否属于艺术**：一部分人认为AI生成音乐缺乏艺术性，而另一部分人则认为它可以在某些场景下发挥作用。
• **AI对音乐创作的影响是积极还是消极**：有些人认为AI会带来“有机”文化的复兴，而另一些人则担心AI会取代真人艺术家，使得创作变得肤浅和无意义。

data.title: US Coast Guard Report on Titan Submersible
data.author: rwmj
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OceanGate的TITAN潜艇事故原因及其背后的决策和文化问题

不同观点：
• dwheeler：事故的主要原因是物理因素，包括使用未经认证的碳纤维复合材料用于深海潜水器。报告指出，碳纤维在深海高压环境下承受压应力时表现不佳，且没有获得任何国家或国际标准的认可。此外，人為决策，如公司安全文化的缺失和管理层的傲慢态度，也是导致事故的重要原因。
• TheCleric：此次事故是"快速行动、打破常规"和"反对监管"文化的逻辑结果。许多安全规则都是基于血的教训写成的，并非无意义的官僚主义。OceanGate忽视了这些规则，导致了悲剧的发生。
• post_break：尽管潜艇的设计和材料有诸多缺陷，如碳纤维和控制器的缺陷，但它在前几次航行中幸存了下来。Stockton Rush忽视了警告信号，最终导致了事故的发生。
• cogman10：调查显示潜艇的实时监控系统发出了警告，但OceanGate没有采取行动。他们不仅忽视了数据，也没有进行预防性维护或妥善储存潜艇，这是严重的管理失误。
• ItsBob：从Netflix纪录片中了解到，事故发生时乘客在毫秒级别内瞬间消失，这种极端的物理现象让人感到震惊和不可思议。
• ridgeguy：纤维增强复合材料在拉伸时表现出色，但在压缩时表现极差。选择这种材料用于潜艇设计从一开始就是个错误。
• ortusdux：美国海岸警卫队的听证会，尤其是Matthew McCoy的证词，揭示了公司内部的许多问题，提供了有价值的背景信息。
• bouchard：Stockton Rush希望像SpaceX在太空领域一样，成为海洋探索领域的颠覆者。然而，他的冒险精神最终导致了灾难。
• Luker88：作为消费者，是否需要自己对海洋探险公司进行背景调查？海洋工业似乎缺乏监管，或者公司无视规则，这都是令人担忧的问题。
• nathan_compton：事故既有悲剧性，也有讽刺意味。Rush的墓志铭可以写上"快速行动、打破常规"。
• danjl：OceanGate的商业模式基于认为现有法规和设计限制过于保守，最终导致了客户的死亡代价。
• nodesocket：碳纤维在多次测试中表现不佳，其他深水潜艇使用钛材是有原因的。Rush坚持使用碳纤维是不合理的。

补充讨论：
• kelseyfrog：提到"这将成为一个切斯特顿式的围栏"，暗示未来人们可能会从这次事故中吸取教训，建立新的安全规则和标准。

争议焦点：
• 碳纤维材料是否适合用于深海潜艇的争论。
• OceanGate管理层对安全警告的忽视以及对传统安全规则的蔑视。
• 消费者在参与高风险活动时应承担的责任以及行业监管的有效性。

data.title: Ask HN: Have you ever regretted open-sourcing something?
data.author: paulwilsonn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目的利弊与个人经历

不同观点：
• **开源项目的商业化潜力**：
  - [Aurornis] 提到见过开源项目创建者后悔没有将其商业化，认为如果项目闭源并商业化可能会带来财富。
  - [bob1029] 主张对复杂产品采取源代码可见但收费的模式，认为开源不一定适合所有类型的软件。

• **开源项目带来的负面体验**：
  - [pentamassiv] 描述了自己维护的开源项目被大公司使用，但申请该公司的职位却被拒绝，感到错失了受益于自己劳动成果的机会。
  - [erulabs] 分享了自己在年轻时因开源代码质量差而受到批评，导致长时间失去编码欲望。
  - [doawoo] 提到开源项目带来了经济资助，但也引发了其他开发者的嫉妒和无理要求。
  - [blibble] 后悔开源了自己的作品，因为它们被AI技术使用而没有得到应有的 attribution（署名）。
  - [acheong08] 后悔开源了一个个人项目，因为其他用户利用其功能绕过官方限制，最终导致项目失效。
  - [throwaway889900] 因未满足用户需求而收到死亡威胁，决定退出开源。

• **开源项目的法律与公司限制**：
  - [aurumque] 描述了自己努力争取公司开源一个工具，但因公司限制无法维护项目，最终对开源感到失望。
  - [greyface-] 试图通过公司审核委员会开源个人项目，但因程序繁琐和不确定的知识产权问题而放弃。

• **开源项目的维护负担**：
  - [ptmcc] 提到自己开源的项目收到过多的功能请求和不合理的bug报告，导致对分享个人项目感到不满。
  - [incomingpain] 指出开源项目带来的维护负担和用户需求使得开发者难以长期维护多个项目。

补充讨论：
• **开源项目与误解**：
  - [TheTon] 分享了自己项目被误认为是Google产品而引起广泛关注的经历，质疑这种误解是否是Google Code关闭的原因。
  
• **开源项目的侵权问题**：
  - [galad87] 提到自己以GPL2许可发布的代码被他人稍作修改后在Mac App Store上出售，显示了开源项目可能遭遇的侵权问题。

争议焦点：
• 开源项目的商业化与社区贡献之间的矛盾。
• 开源项目带来的负面体验与开发者期望之间的差距。
• 开源项目在法律、公司政策和个人利益之间的复杂关系。

data.title: SAML Shield: Drop-in protection that works for any stack
data.author: CoffeeOnWrite
data.article_summary: SAML Shield是一款开源安全工具，旨在保护SAML单点登录（SSO）系统免受漏洞和断言攻击。它兼容任何语言或系统，无需更改身份提供者（IdP）设置，可直接嵌入现有SAML栈中，实时验证并阻止恶意断言。SAML Shield能防御多种已知协议级攻击，如签名包装和重放攻击，并提供集中化日志和回测支持（即将推出）。用户可以选择自行部署开源版本或使用Stytch管理版本，以获得自动更新和零维护的安全保障。通过简单的API调用即可集成，支持多种部署选项如cURL、Node.js、Python和NGINX。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SAMLShield工具的优缺点及其在安全防护中的作用

不同观点：
• mooreds（Stytch竞争对手的员工）认为SAMLShield的开源版本和文档有帮助，清晰标明了功能限制，并且定价透明。然而，他指出该工具不是一劳永逸的解决方案，特别是在处理加密SAML声明和防重放攻击方面存在局限性。他还提到理解该工具的安全覆盖范围很重要。

data.title: FCC abandons efforts to make U.S. broadband fast and affordable
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: 文章简要总结了美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）委员卡尔提出的一项提案。该提案援引了最高法院的一项裁决，该裁决限制了联邦机构解释模糊法律的能力。根据这一裁决，卡尔认为最谨慎的做法是严格遵循法律文本。文章批评特朗普政府在此问题上的自利态度：如果某政策对政府有利，他们全力支持；如果不利，则置之不理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国宽带扩展和改善的有效性及方法

不同观点：
• **Stego-tech** 认为，自2000年代以来，数十亿美元的宽带扩展资金大多被大型电信公司吸收，但这些公司未能有效扩展宽带、提高速度或降低价格，资金最终变成了这些公司的利润。他主张通过资助市政宽带来为私营企业提供竞争基础，但这一方案因说客的阻挠而未能实现。

• **Db48x** 则认为，当前100Mbps的宽带定义已经足够，因为目前没有需要超过20Mbps的“杀手级应用”。例如，4K流媒体只需要16Mbps，因此提高到1Gbps只是“锦上添花”，而非必要。FCC仍在为未服务地区安装电缆或光纤的项目提供资助，但不要求每个用户必须拥有1Gbps的服务。

• **Consumer451** 提供了一个欧盟的例子，指出在欧盟国家，农村地区已经实现了高速光纤网络，且价格低廉。这得益于欧盟的资金支持，显示了政府补贴对宽带扩展的有效性。

• **Esaym** 对卫星互联网（如Starlink和亚马逊的计划）持乐观态度，认为这可能比为农村家庭铺设有线互联网更具成本效益。同时，他认为手机网络已基本覆盖了互联网接入的空白。

• **Ethagknight** 认为，随着光纤网络和5G的扩展以及卫星网络的显著改善，是否每个美国房产都需要光纤连接值得商榷。他还指出，FCC并未实现“负担得起”的目标，电信公司从中获得了巨额利润。

补充讨论：
• **BrenBarn** 提出一个激进的观点，认为需要对当前的权力结构进行彻底变革，才能解决宽带问题。他描述了一种理想情况，即通过大规模没收从当前困境中获利的实体资产来重建更公平的体系。

• **Andrex** 和 **User94wjwuid** 强调了市政互联网规则的解除和电信垄断难以打破的问题，认为电信公司享有特权，而普通消费者则受到不公平对待。

• **Bryanrasmussen** 讽刺地指出，尽管宽带问题未得到解决，但可能会看到一些宣传声称美国宽带是世界上最快速和最负担得起的。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于是否需要提高宽带速度标准和扩展光纤网络，以及政府和私营企业各自应在宽带扩展中扮演何种角色。一方认为现有标准足够，另一方则主张通过市政宽带或其他方式进行更广泛的扩展。此外，卫星互联网的兴起也为宽带扩展提供了新的可能性，但其可行性和长期影响仍存在争议。

data.title: Small changes that made our daily stand-ups more useful
data.author: dkoprowski
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何改善敏捷开发中的每日站会，使其更具价值而非流于形式或浪费时间。站会常被视为负担，因其容易变成冗长的状态报告，使参与者感到无聊且缺乏实际帮助。作者通过实践，提出了一些有效利用站会的建议：

1. **站会的真正目的**：应聚焦于同步当天的计划和优先事项，尽早发现障碍，鼓励团队协作和知识共享，增强团队责任感和支持。
   
2. **常见陷阱**：避免陷入“报告模式”和知识孤岛，报告模式导致枯燥、脱离和错失协作机会；知识孤岛则让重要信息无法共享。

3. **实际例子**：通过具体例子展示如何改进站会发言，使其更具针对性、上下文背景，并专注于当天的目标和需求，促进团队协作。

最终，站会应成为团队协作、支持和解决问题的起点，而非单纯的状态汇报。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：每日站会的有效性和实施方式

不同观点：
• **站会的微管理问题**：[agentultra] 认为每日站会是微管理的核心，只有在没有经理参与的情况下才可能有效，只是团队成员交流需要完成的任务。
• **重复和社交压力**：[hshdhdhj4444] 指出，站会上的障碍和延迟信息已经在团队聊天中提到过。此外，社交压力使得承认自己没做多少变得困难。建议将进度报告会议减少到1-2次每周。
• **关注当下和障碍**：[SoftTalker] 强调站会不应回顾昨天，只需讨论今天的计划和任何障碍。
• **会议时长问题**：[CER10TY] 提到他们的站会从未少于60分钟，质疑如何在15分钟内完成。
• **异步沟通的有效性**：[neilv] 认为站会内容可以通过异步沟通完成，并提供了一个异步更新示例，认为这样更及时有效。
• **跳过站会**：[ok123456] 直接跳过站会。
• **以问题和障碍为中心**：[pan69] 说明他们的站会专注于提出问题和障碍，而不是个人状态更新，有时会议只需要2-3分钟。
• **以工作为中心的站会**：[scott_w] 建议从以人为中心转变为以工作为中心的站会，按工作进展顺序讨论，这样更快并能集中于解决问题。
• **详细汇报的必要性**：[sda2] 认为如果不详细汇报昨天做了什么，如何证明自己的工作价值并避免被裁。
• **通过工具进行站会更新**：[captainkrtek] 描述他们的团队通过Slack机器人进行每日更新，包括已完成、下一步计划和任何障碍，管理层可以查看并跟进。
• **SPUR议程模板**：[dctoedt] 建议使用SPUR（状态、计划、不确定性、报告）作为站会议程模板，帮助组织讨论。
• **站会无用论**：[theboywho] 认为站会无用，开发人员需要频繁同步工作，障碍应立即提出，站会浪费时间。站会若被认为有用，可能是参与者本身有问题。
• **通过咖啡角聚焦讨论**：[Okkef] 提到在“早上好”虚拟咖啡角后，通过快速提问帮助团队聚焦重要事项，如今日计划、障碍和需要帮助的地方。

补充讨论：
• 站会的核心目的应是快速同步和解决障碍，而非个人状态汇报。
• 站会的时长和频率是争议焦点，建议通过异步沟通、工具辅助或改变会议形式来提高效率。
• 站会的有效性与团队文化和实施方式密切相关，不同团队有不同的需求和挑战。

44800943.article_content:
Share
Daily stand-ups are a cornerstone of agile software development – but often they’re seen as a burden or a distraction. Why? Because they frequently devolve into long status reports that bore participants and add little real value.
Others see it as a waste of time or such regular part of their day, that it doesn’t deserve a second though.
During the past two years, together with my team, I worked on improving our daily to transform it to a tool that helps every participant to kickstart their day. In this blogpost I share tips that might be useful also for your team.
What Is the Purpose of a Daily Meeting – and What It Isn’t
I often see complains on developers forums that a daily meetings are used only as a control mechanism – a way for managers to check up on what everyone did yesterday.
Since I trust my team, I’ve designed our daily meetings to bring real value to developers.
Instead of treating the daily as a status report, we use it as a chance for:
syncing plans
and priorities for the current day,
signaling blockers
early so the team can help,
encouraging
collaboration
and
knowledge sharing
,
building a sense of
team ownership
and support.
I don’t want a daily meeting where everyone focuses on yesterday. I want one where we help each other move forward.
While it’s tempting to ditch the “what I did yesterday” report entirely to avoid turning meetings into monotonous recaps,
don’t abandon it completely
.
Question about yesterday can reveal dysfunctions or blocker early, like when team members admit, “I didn’t get much done due to back-to-back meetings,” signaling a need for broader changes to free up focus time. My point is to
keep it brief and tie it to today’s plans
for maximum value.
The purpose of a daily meeting is to collaboratively kickstart the day by aligning individual plans with team goals, supporting each other, and uncovering blockers.
Common Pitfalls: Reporting Mode and Knowledge Silos
Many teams get stuck in the “reporting mode,” where each developer spends most of their time describing their own yesterday’s work, often justifying themselves.
This leads to:
Monotony:
Hearing detailed reports every day gets boring fast.
Disengagement:
People stop listening or multitask in background.
Missed collaboration:
Blockers and requests for help don’t get surfaced.
Knowledge silos:
Important insights stay locked inside individuals.
That is my biggest nemesis
. I always felt that purely reporting meetings are a burden, a waste of energy, those are spreading mistrust in the team. It might work in some setups – I don’t deny that there is a use case. Although, in a workflow that I value, I wanted to have a meeting, where we plan the upcoming day to spend the time productive.
Real-World Daily Stand-Up Examples
Avoid: The Classic “Justifying My Existence” Update
Read through this daily status update and think how could it be improved:
Yesterday, I fixed a bug assigned to me. Then, I attended all-hands meeting and I had to go out for some time. Then we had retro. I also started a new story from to-do. Today, I will continue working on it.
Key Issues:
Vague:
No specific details on what was fixed or which story was started.
No Context:
Generic terms like “assigned to me,” “new story,” and “continue working on it” do not provide actionable info. What story that dev is even mentioning? No one knows.
No Request for Help:
No mention of needing assistance or collaboration.
No Value for Team:
Update is mostly a personal log; teammates cannot offer help or gain insight.
Focused on Past:
Update is mostly a report on yesterday’s activities, not today’s goals or blockers.
After listening to such update, teammates wouldn’t think of how they could collaborate. They would be lost, forced to ask additional questions or simply fall back and wait for the next person.
Improved: A Specific, Team-Focused Daily Update
Here is my attempt to improve such update:
Yesterday, I fixed a sidebar flickering bug. Please review my PR soon as it is annoying for customers. I started a video player story that we discussed at the last refinement. Since it’s my first time working with the player module, I’d appreciate pairing up or any tips from someone familiar with it.
Today, my focus is on wiring up the play/pause functionality. Happy to sync after stand-up if anyone’s available.
What’s Improved:
Specific:
Names the details of bug and story.
Contextual:
Explains the urgency (“annoying for customers”) and the origin of the story (“discussed at last refinement”).
Focus on Today:
Highlights what is planned for today and where support is needed.
Expressed openness:
Invites help both for pairing and advice–not just passive review.
Offered a sync:
Proactively asks for a follow-up, lowering the barrier for collaboration.
Additionally, when a Jira board (or whatever you use) is on a shared display the team should have no problem with following what this dev is talking about and how to help them.
How We Structure Our Daily Meetings to Create Val
44800943.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何改善敏捷开发中的每日站会，使其更具价值而非流于形式或浪费时间。站会常被视为负担，因其容易变成冗长的状态报告，使参与者感到无聊且缺乏实际帮助。作者通过实践，提出了一些有效利用站会的建议：

1. **站会的真正目的**：应聚焦于同步当天的计划和优先事项，尽早发现障碍，鼓励团队协作和知识共享，增强团队责任感和支持。
   
2. **常见陷阱**：避免陷入“报告模式”和知识孤岛，报告模式导致枯燥、脱离和错失协作机会；知识孤岛则让重要信息无法共享。

3. **实际例子**：通过具体例子展示如何改进站会发言，使其更具针对性、上下文背景，并专注于当天的目标和需求，促进团队协作。

最终，站会应成为团队协作、支持和解决问题的起点，而非单纯的状态汇报。

• **重复和社交压力**：[hshdhdhj4444] 指出，站会上的障碍和延迟信息已经在团队聊天中提到过。此外，社交压力使得承认自己没做多少变得困难。建议将进度报告会议减少到1-2次每周。

data.title: Google agrees to pause AI workloads when power demand spikes
data.author: twapi
data.article_summary: Google宣布，将在电力需求高峰时暂停非必要的AI工作负载，以保护电网。这一举措是在与印第安纳密歇根电力公司和田纳西流域管理局达成协议后做出的。在炎热夏季，居民大量使用空调导致电网压力增加时，若能源需求激增或电网出现问题，Google将通过调整数据中心耗电量或延迟非紧急任务来减少电力使用，这一过程称为“需求响应”。尽管AI模型训练耗电巨大，但一些工作负载无需全天候运行，可以在电网压力较小时进行。Google还在投资可再生能源和核能，以应对数据中心耗电问题。不过，Google无法随意暂停云客户的AI任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电力需求响应、人工智能（AI）公司的能源消耗及其对社会和环境的影响

不同观点：
• [acc_297] 认为，当前我们过快地增加了电力消耗，尤其是在实现碳强度减少目标之前，推动了大规模的电力需求。担忧市场力量无法有效监管跨国科技公司，这些公司可以几乎不受限制地选择数据中心的地点，并将计算基础设施的外部性转移到远离付费客户的地方。

• [kerblang] 强调“需求响应”是电力公司和大型客户之间长期存在的做法，不仅仅是针对工业用户，普通消费者也可以通过使用电力公司提供的自动调节温控器，在高峰负荷期间减少用电，并获得折扣。

• [HocusLocus] 指出，AI公司正试图通过公开讨论其对电网电力需求的影响，来展示自己作为“良好的企业管理者”。然而，北美地区依赖天然气和石油能源，拒绝核能，这将导致问题。AI公司不仅没有创造直接的就业机会，反而因其能源消耗引发更多的反对，最终可能被迫迁离城市，甚至最终可能被驱赶到“轨道上”。

• [Pet_Ant] 提出，如果AI训练仅在电力过剩时进行，并取代类似比特币挖矿的能源浪费行为，可能对社会产生积极影响。

• [codemac] 认为，数据中心（DC）运营商普遍与当地电网有需求响应协议，并且在风暴或需求增加期间与上游电力供应商密切合作，极少会危害整个社区的电网安全。对数据中心运营的担忧往往是过度紧张的表现。

• [im3w1l] 关注AI训练中的电力成本，认为电力成本可能已经超过芯片折旧成本，成为主要的训练开支。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是AI公司是否在通过展示对能源问题的关注来提升其企业形象，而实际上这些公司对当地能源基础设施和环境带来了负面影响（HocusLocus的观点）。
• 另一个讨论点是，电力需求响应机制在工业用户和普通消费者之间的应用是否公平，以及如何在全球范围内有效监管跨国科技公司的能源消耗（acc_297和kerblang的观点）。
• 对AI训练能源消耗的未来影响和解决方案的探讨，包括将其与比特币挖矿进行类比，提出利用过剩电力进行训练的潜在益处（Pet_Ant的观点）。
• 对电力成本在AI训练中的重要性及其对行业的影响进行了简要分析（im3w1l的观点）。

Google agrees to pause AI workloads to protect the grid when power demand spikes
19
On hot summer days, air conditioning is rather more important than search summaries
Tobias Mann
Mon 4 Aug 2025
//
22:58 UTC
Google will pause non-essential AI workloads to protect power grids, the advertising giant announced on Monday.
The web giant already does this sort of thing for non-essential workloads like processing YouTube vids, which it moves to datacenters where power is available rather than continuing to run them in places demand for energy strains the grid.
Under an agreement with Indiana Michigan Power (I&M) and the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), Google will use the same techniques for AI workloads.
The announcement comes as states served by the power companies brace for a heat wave that will likely strain the grid as residents use air conditioners and increase demand for energy. Amid debate about datacenters’ consumption of power and water, the last thing that the Chocolate Factory needs is folks blaming its AI Mode search function for a power outage when temperatures top 100°F (37.7°C).
Under the agreement, if energy demand surges or there's a disruption in the grid due to extreme weather, I&M and TVA can now request that Google reduce its power use by rescheduling workloads or limiting non-urgent tasks until the issue is resolved.
By dynamically adjusting how much power its bit barns are allowed to consume, a process Google calls “demand response”, the web giant argues that new datacenters can be interconnected more quickly — presumably because utilities are less concerned about them causing brown outs or outages.
"By including load flexibility in our overall energy plan, we can manage AI-driven growth even where power generation and transmission are constrained," Google wrote in a
blog post
on Monday.
Training and running AI models can easily consume tens or even hundreds of megawatts of power for hours, days, or weeks at a time, depending on how big or complex they are. However certain workloads don't need to run 24/7. Advancements in checkpointing mean that a model could be trained exclusively at night when grid capacity is at its greatest.
Datacenter demand-response is still a nascent technology and is only being employed at a handful of Google bit barns. Further complicating the matter, the approach is also incompatible with certain high-demand workloads, such as Search, Maps, or its cloud business, Google notes.
AI going critical: Hyundai to help build nuclear-powered datacenter in Texas
Tony Blair Institute: UK needs bit barns to lead in AI deployment, not training
Altman embraces inner Viking, raids Europe with 100K GPU supercluster in Norway
Datacenter lobby blows a fuse over EU efficiency proposals
Google may have the ability to spin down its own machine learning workloads as it pleases, but it can't exactly pause its cloud customers' AI jobs without causing a few headaches.
Demand-response isn't the only way Google is looking to curb the power demands of its AI infrastructure build out, and it's not hard to see why. The search giant
plowed
$14 billion into servers in just 91 days of its 2025 fiscal year with plans to spend upwards of $85 billion by year's end.
The company also continues to invest in alternative energy sources, including geothermal, solar, wind, hydroelectric, and nuclear. Google aims to
field
small modular reactors just as soon as they get their hands on one, and in May
signed
an agreement with Elementl Power to support the development of three potential reactor sites in the US. ®

data.title: Show HN: Stagewise (YC S25) – Front end coding agent for existing codebases
data.author: juliangoetze
data.article_summary: Stagewise是首个用于生产级web应用的前端编码代理。它运行于浏览器中，能直接修改本地代码库，支持多种框架和设置。开发者无需繁琐操作，只需通过点击元素和输入指令，即可让stagewise自动完成更改。它提供插件定制功能，并且开源，采用AGPL-3.0许可证。使用时，开发者只需在项目根目录运行指定命令即可启动stagewise，无需额外安装。同时，它支持多种代理工具集成，如Cursor、GitHub Copilot等。社区和支持渠道包括Discord和GitHub issues。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对产品的评价及功能建议，以及对产品竞争力和应用场景的讨论。

不同观点：

data.title: White House Orders NASA to Destroy Important Satellite
data.author: 42lux
data.article_summary: 《白宫指示NASA终止两项专注于气候变化的卫星任务，即轨道碳观测台（Orbiting Carbon Observatories）。这些卫星负责收集二氧化碳数据，对油气公司和农业有重要作用。其中一个附属于国际空间站，另一个是独立卫星，若任务终止将在大气中烧毁。特朗普政府此举被认为是其否认气候变化立场的一部分，尽管这些任务每年仅花费1500万美元，且数据质量极高。终止这些任务引发了科学界的愤怒，并可能违反现有预算法。国会议员提出反击方案，以维持NASA预算，并警告终止地球观测任务将严重影响对天气和气候灾难的应对能力。》

44799468.article_content:
Image by
NASA / Futurism
The White House has instructed NASA employees to terminate two major, climate change-focused satellite missions.
As
NPR
reports
, Trump officials reached out to the space agency to draw up plans for terminating the two missions, called the Orbiting Carbon Observatories. They've been collecting widely-used data, providing both oil and gas companies and farmers with detailed information about the distribution of carbon dioxide and how it can affect crop health.
One is attached to the International Space Station, and the other is collecting data as a stand-alone satellite. The latter would meet its permanent demise after burning up in the atmosphere if the mission were to be terminated.
We can only speculate as to why the Trump administration wants to end the missions. But considering president Donald Trump's
staunch climate change denial
and his administration's efforts to deal the agency's science directorate a
potentially existential blow
, it's not difficult to speculate.
Worse yet, the two observatories had been expected to function for many more years, scientists working on them told
NPR
. A
2023 review
by NASA concluded that the data they'd been providing had been "of exceptionally high quality."
The observatories provide detailed carbon dioxide measurements across various locations, allowing scientists to get a detailed glimpse of how human activity is affecting greenhouse gas emissions.
Former NASA employee David Crisp, who worked on the Orbiting Carbon Observatories' instruments, told
NPR
that current staffers reached out to him.
"They were asking me very sharp questions," he said. "The only thing that would have motivated those questions was [that] somebody told them to come up with a termination plan."
Crisp said it "makes no economic sense to terminate NASA missions that are returning incredibly valuable data," pointing out it costs only $15 million per year to maintain both observatories, a tiny fraction of the agency's $25.4 billion budget.
Other scientists who've used data from the missions have also been asked questions related to terminating the missions.
The two observatories are only two of
dozens of space missions
facing existential threats in the form of the Trump administration's proposed 2026 fiscal year budget. Countless scientists have been outraged by the proposal,
arguing
it could precipitate an end to the United States' leadership in space.
Lawmakers have since drawn up a counteroffer that would keep NASA's budget roughly in line with this year's.
"We rejected cuts that would have devastated NASA science by 47 percent and would have terminated 55 operating and planned missions," said senator and top appropriator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) in a July statement, as
quoted by
Bloomberg
.
Simply terminating Earth-monitoring missions to pursue an anti-science agenda could be a massive self-own, lawmakers say — and potentially breaking laws as well by overriding existing, allocated budgets.
"Eliminating funds or scaling down the operations of Earth-observing satellites would be catastrophic and would severely impair our ability to forecast, manage, and respond to severe weather and climate disasters," House representative and Committee on Science, Space and Technology ranking member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) told
NPR
.
"The Trump administration is forcing the proposed cuts in its FY26 budget request on already appropriated FY25 funds," she added. "This is illegal."

data.title: Why is GitHub UI getting slower?
data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: 本文主要抱怨GitHub用户界面近年来变得越来越慢，尤其是页面切换和加载时间过长的问题。作者通过开发者工具分析发现，使用Turbo预加载的页面切换本应是性能优化，但实际表现却比直接打开新标签页还慢两倍。客户端的后处理时间甚至比从服务器加载HTML还长，导致整体体验不佳。此外，新的加载条进一步提醒用户界面速度的缓慢。作者批评这种客户端路由比完整页面重载还慢的现象，并指出在大型PR中浏览时界面会冻结几秒，可能与渲染过多DOM节点有关。最后，作者质疑GitHub是否会根据其路线图改善性能问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub的性能和用户体验问题，尤其是在使用React重写后的表现。

不同观点：
• xPaw和astrolx认为，GitHub自使用React重写以来性能显著下降，页面加载和渲染速度变慢，影响了用户查看差异的体验。astrolx甚至因此迁移到了自托管的Forgejo实例。
• bapak指出，GitHub可能雇佣了许多初级前端开发人员，导致当前的UI问题，尽管之前的AJAX实现也有批评，但至少更接近于基本的HTML和HTTP。
• Vegenoid表示，看到其他人也有同样的感受感到欣慰，认为大型工程组织为了证明自己的存在价值而进行不必要的更改，导致了软件质量的下降。
• 0xTJ提供了一个反例，McMaster-Carr网站因其简洁和静态的页面设计而非常快，尽管其与GitHub有不同的使用场景。
• pushcx详细描述了GitHub上出现的各种SPA（单页应用）问题，如页面样式丢失、状态不刷新等，并提到使用jujutsu替代Git的体验，认为GitHub需要在UI设计上进行大改。
• brunojppb认为GitHub的iOS应用表现良好，希望Web UI也能有同样的性能。
• konstruktors将GitHub的UI问题与Facebook的UI相比较，认为React和客户端渲染逻辑是问题根源。
• gimenete表示正在开发githero.app来解决GitHub的性能问题，并透露曾在GitHub工作三年，公司内部已经意识到这些问题但改进不明显。
• nkrisc指出符号浏览器功能影响了浏览器的后退按钮功能，导致用户体验问题。
• Starlevel004认为GitHub的代码查看器对长文件的支持很差，质疑GitHub的开发团队是否自己使用产品。
• butz提到GitHub坚持使用React，而Edge正在因性能问题迁移到web组件。
• coffeebeqn认为GitHub的问题与其他微软的Web服务类似，都是缓慢且体验差。
• rwrrll主张将GitHub回滚到2012年的版本，只保留基本功能以提高速度和可靠性。

补充讨论：
• GitHub性能下降的具体表现包括页面加载慢、渲染错误、状态不刷新等。
• 讨论中多次提到React和SPA架构对性能和用户体验的影响。
• 一些用户提出了迁移到其他平台或工具的实际案例或建议，如Forgejo、jujutsu。
• 有用户质疑GitHub内部是否对其产品进行充分的用户测试和质量控制。

争议焦点：
• GitHub使用React重写是否是导致性能下降的主要原因。
• 是否应回滚到以前的版本以恢复速度和可靠性。

44799861.article_content:
I couldn't help but notice - GitHub UI has been getting slower and slower recently. Some things that were snappy before are
hellishly slow nowadays. GitHub is doing something weird and I just can't wrap my head around what's going on there.
You guys developing at GitHub, you're using GitHub to develop it, right? Do you not see this? What's going on?
Whenever I bump into slow website which drives me nuts, I open the devtools and profile it. Who knows, maybe I
find something to report and the problem will get fixed.
To give one representative example, here's a profile for switching from "Conversation" tab to
"Files changed" tab on a PR.
Before we look into the profile, notice that this takes over 5s. How is anything like that acceptable in 2025 is beyond me.
Now, if you dive deep into this, you'll see that GitHub uses
Turbo
to preload next page and swap out the
content without page reload. This is usually done as a performance optimization, but here, we see something completely
absurd.
If you try this out at home and play around with it, you'll find out that
opening the "Files changed" link in a new tab is
actually 2x faster:
And not only that - the client side post-processing in the first profile actually takes longer than loading the html
from the server. This whole thing just doesn't make any sense.
The cherry on top is the new loading bar that just drives me absolutely nuts, because it reminds me how slow
the whole transition is:
Guys... can you just make the transition fast such that you don't need a new loading bar?
Like, what's the point of doing client side routing, when you just recreate the full page reload experience, but slower?
The whole point of doing SPAs was to avoid this. Client side routing should be instant.
This is just one of many performance problems on GitHub. It didn't use to be that way. Trying to go through multiple PRs and
issues is just suffering now. Imagine you have 20 PRs to find out which one introduced a regression, and every click takes more than 5 seconds to show something.
Don't even get me started on the diff view itself - yes, the one that periodically freezes for 2 seconds while browsing through
large PR's - maybe it has something to do with the fact that it renders thousands of invisible plus buttons with the
same inlined svg icon:
Or, you know, maybe not trying to render
100 000 DOM nodes
in general would
also help.
The whole window freezes for 3 seconds when you resize the dev tools window because you want to profile
this thing.
Does this ever improve?
🔗
So, maybe, when
some of the popular issues
are related to performance, and GitHub has this seemingly related
"Platform collaboration at scale"
focus area in the roadmap, maybe this will change?
Let's look at the roadmap and see if we can find
anything
related
to
performance
. Did you find something?

• gimenete表示正在开发githero.app来解决GitHub的性能问题，并透露曾在GitHub工作三年，公司内部已经意识到这些问题但改进不明显。
• nkrisc指出符号浏览器功能影响了浏览器的后退按钮功能，导致用户体验问题。
• Starlevel004认为GitHub的代码查看器对长文件的支持很差，质疑GitHub的开发团队是否自己使用产品。
• butz提到GitHub坚持使用React，而Edge正在因性能问题迁移到web组件。
• coffeebeqn认为GitHub的问题与其他微软的Web服务类似，都是缓慢且体验差。
• rwrrll主张将GitHub回滚到2012年的版本，只保留基本功能以提高速度和可靠性。

补充讨论：
• GitHub性能下降的具体表现包括页面加载慢、渲染错误、状态不刷新等。
• 讨论中多次提到React和SPA架构对性能和用户体验的影响。
• 一些用户提出了迁移到其他平台或工具的实际案例或建议，如Forgejo、jujutsu。
• 有用户质疑GitHub内部是否对其产品进行充分的用户测试和质量控制。

争议焦点：
• GitHub使用React重写是否是导致性能下降的主要原因。
• 是否应回滚到以前的版本以恢复速度和可靠性。

Writing
Gate-level emulation of an Intel 4004 in 4004 bytes of C
by
Nicholas Carlini
2025-08-04
The International Obfuscated C Code Contest results were announced this last weekend,
and I was thrilled to see that
my entry
was among the winners.
In this article I want to walk through what it is:
a feature-complete gate-level emulator for the Intel 4004 that's capable of emulating the original
Busicom 141-pf calculator ROM---the application for which the 4004 was originally designed.
To make things exciting, this program doesn't emulate the 4004 the "normal" way.
Instead, this program is actually just a logic gate simulator, but where I've designed an entire
4004 as circuit (microcoded for space!) that's embedded in the program and then emulated.
And because we're 50 years in the future, this gate-level emulated calculator
runs at a few hundred instructions per second which
is actually fast enough to be usable, just as long as you're not in a hurry.
This is part two in a two (or maybe three?) part series of posts.
Last time
,
I explained the design of
miniHDL
,
a small python DSL that allows you to build and design circuits.
This time, I'm going to use miniHDL to design my 4004 (along with an intel 4003,
4002, and 4001), and then write some scaffolding so that it has the correct "hardware" to
run the original program ROM,
and then somehow crush a 15,000 byte program and 200,000 byte circuit into the below <4004 bytes.
Source code, as always, is on GitHub.

data.title: Wikipedia ordered by Portuguese courts to censor articles and provide user data
data.author: tiagod
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了维基媒体基金会（WMF）相关的社区讨论页面，旨在促进社区与基金会之间的沟通与协调。该页面用于发布和讨论信息、提案、反馈请求等重要事项，但WMF并不将其视为正式沟通渠道。涉及基金会较少关注的提案或技术问题的讨论应在其他特定页面进行。该页面不适合用于对文章内容的申诉、紧急报告或个人攻击，不当言论可能被删除。

文章还提到一个关于WMF在Roblox上发布游戏的讨论，该游戏使用了生成式AI制作的图片，引发社区对WMF环保承诺与实际行为不一致的质疑。有用户认为此举主要针对年轻群体，是WMF尝试吸引新受众的实验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：维基媒体葡萄牙分部在面对法律诉讼时删除有关文章的决定及其后果

不同观点：
• tetromino_ 认为，维基媒体应该抵抗葡萄牙当局的要求，保留文章内容不变，并关闭维基媒体葡萄牙分部以示抗议。他们认为此决定展示了面对法律威胁时屈服的错误示范，可能会引发更多类似的诉讼。
• tiagod 提供了有关事件的背景信息，包括之前关于此事的讨论链接和关于战略性诉讼（SLAPP）的解释，但没有明确表达支持或反对删除文章的立场，而是提供了相关资料以供进一步了解。
• SilverElfin 对文章删除持保留态度，关注点在于如果有人被诽谤，该如何追究责任，是对维基百科本身还是对贡献者。同时，他们提出了如何识别贡献者身份的实际问题。

补充讨论：
• tetromino_ 的评论中包含情绪化的言辞，如“short sighted cowards”和“infamous assholes”，显示出对维基媒体决策的强烈不满。
• SilverElfin 提出了关于法律程序和责任追究的实际问题，显示出对维基百科如何处理诽谤指控的关注，这涉及到平台责任和用户隐私保护的复杂关系。
• tiagod 的评论主要是信息分享，帮助其他讨论者了解更多背景信息，尤其是关于SLAPP的解释，这有助于理解法律背景。

争议焦点：
• 维基媒体葡萄牙分部删除文章的决定是否合理，是否会引发更多的法律诉讼。
• 如何在保护用户隐私和追究诽谤责任之间取得平衡。

总结：讨论主要围绕维基媒体葡萄牙分部在法律压力下的应对措施是否适当，以及如何在法律诉讼中处理诽谤指控和用户隐私问题。各方对维基媒体的决策、法律程序及平台责任有不同的看法和关注点。

Official Wikipedia Roblox game and Generative AI use

]
I considered whether to add this as a subsection to the above RFC on WMF AI development, but decided not to as I didn't want to further bloat that discussion. Regardless, just earlier today I came across a
post on instagram
from the official Wikipedia instagram account (
facebook link
for boomers who don't have instagram) showcasing a new Wikipedia
Roblox
game. The post was made almost two weeks ago so I'm not sure whether it has already been discussed before, but this is a continuation of the use of generative AI (the cover image for the game page, which is also included in the instagram and facebook posts is almost certainly AI) which has quite openly been discussed and decried by many users in the community. I also think that this is a different issue, though, as rather than this use of AI being even remotely justifiable as trying to improve the quality of the 'pedia, the use of generative AI images in what is basically
marketing materials
really only serves to costs while providing a worse product. I also echo users concerns about the WMF's environmentalism when they say things like
The Wikimedia Foundation believes that a long-term commitment to sustainability is an essential component of our work towards the Wikimedia mission and vision

data.title: Ask HN: Why Did Mercurial Die?:(
data.author: sergiotapia
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Git与Mercurial版本控制工具的流行原因及两者之间的竞争

不同观点：
• WorldMaker：认为Git的流行部分归因于网络效应，以及Mercurial早期受到反Python情绪的影响。Python 2到3的过渡问题进一步加剧了这种反感情绪。
• marklar423：Git的初始流行产生了复合效应，使其超越Mercurial。在2010年左右，Git的支持、文档和社区资源更加丰富，使得切换到Git成为更优选择。FAANG公司中有些仍在使用Mercurial，但它们对整个技术生态影响有限。
• silveira：GitHub和Git在Linux内核开发中的使用是Git流行的重要原因，人们认为既然Git对Linux足够好，那么对其他项目也应该足够好。
• seunosewa：GitHub和Git相互促进流行，主要的Mercurial托管服务停止支持以及Google关闭Google Code加速了Mercurial的衰落。Git的灵活性和功能丰富性使其更受欢迎。
• jonathaneunice：GitHub通过网络效应使Git在团队协作和社交编码中更易用，Bitbucket的支持力度不如GitHub。Git的市场领导地位使其在支持服务中更受青睐，类似于VHS与Betamax之争。
• manifoldgeo：Mozilla仍在使用Mercurial进行Firefox开发，但正在迁移到Git和GitHub。Mercurial的使用感较为陌生，而Git是行业标准。
• brudgers：认为Git和Mercurial都是足够好的工具，工程实践中“足够好”是核心。初学者缺乏经验，对工具的选择不敏感。生态系统和品牌效应（如GitHub和Linus Torvalds的背书）是关键。
• ectospheno：Mercurial在大型仓库上曾经非常慢，虽然后来有了很大改进，但早期的问题影响了其采用。
• dehrmann：GitHub的影响是一个因素，Linus Torvalds的支持也是Git流行的重要原因，并非纯粹出于技术理由。
• romanhn：Facebook仍在使用Mercurial，GitHub是Git最终胜出的原因，使其成为默认选择。
• billy99k：因技术问题（如bug和崩溃）无法解决而从Mercurial转向Git。
• xeromal：GitHub提供了免费的私有仓库托管，促进了Git的流行。
• incomingpain：从Subversion直接转向Git，认为Git的分支功能优于Mercurial。
• gjvc：计算机行业是赢家通吃的行业，胜者往往获得更多市场份额。

补充讨论：
• Git与GitHub的相互促进作用
• Linus Torvalds对Git的背书影响
• Mercurial在大型项目中的性能问题
• GitHub和Git在社区支持、文档和资源上的优势
• Mozilla等组织从Mercurial向Git的迁移过程
• 工程实践中工具选择的标准和考量

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国内政部关于可再生能源的新政策及其影响，以及对气候变化政策的政治争议

不同观点：
• jauntywundrkind和部分其他用户认为，内政部的新政策（要求太阳能或风能项目在联邦土地上的发电密度与煤炭、天然气或核电站相同）几乎使得可再生能源建设变得不可能。他们批评此举是不合理的，并将其视为对国家发展的破坏。
• dehrmann指出，如果没有对外国太阳能板的关税，太阳能可能会更便宜，并认为太阳能已经变得足够便宜，可以独立发展。
• keb_希望有人能为“人类对气候变化没有显著影响”的观点提供有力辩护，表明这一观点在某些群体中得到支持，并与其长期以来相信的科学共识相悖。
• idiotsecant强调，当前问题不仅是太阳能发电，还需要解决储能和传输问题。他们指出，如果储能和传输不足，会导致电力市场不稳定。
• myrmidon批评特朗普的气候政策，认为其政策基于自私、误导信息和对气候变化后果的错误认识，并预测未来人们会视这些立场为明显的愚蠢行为。
• DudeOpotomus和myotheraccount2则认为，特朗普的政策可能是出于愚蠢或腐败，认为其政策基于报复、愚蠢和贿赂。
• avgDev对新政策表示部分理解，虽然不喜欢可再生能源公司的推销方式，但仍支持绿色能源发展，并计划自行安装太阳能板。
• hooverd简单表示支持建设，未展开具体观点。
• EcommerceFlow对两党在太阳能问题上的表现感到失望，认为拜登的补贴政策未能促进太阳能制造业的竞争，并希望特朗普能推出新的补贴以降低制造成本。
• tootie和southernplaces7批评新政策是短视的、出于个人利益和与工业利益相关的动机，认为这种政策不仅反应了经济无知，而且对可再生能源技术的发展有害。
• ujkhsjkdhf234讽刺特朗普通过限制可再生能源发展来为其亿万富翁朋友的税收减免买单。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于内政部新政策对可再生能源发展的限制以及其背后的动机，部分用户认为这是出于对化石燃料行业的保护和对可再生能源的敌视。
• 讨论中还涉及到对气候变化影响的不同看法，以及对特朗普气候政策的广泛批评。
• 用户对储能和传输问题的重要性也有所关注，认为这是当前可再生能源发展中的关键瓶颈。

data.title: Show HN: I spent 6 years building a ridiculous wooden pixel display
data.author: benholmen
data.article_summary:
作者花了六年时间打造了一个不切实际的木制像素显示屏，名为"Kilopixel"，包含1000个像素，任何人都可以通过网站kilopx.com进行绘制。这个项目源于作者对Danny Rozin的非传统镜子和一个每小时播放24帧的电子墨水播放器的兴趣，激发了制作一个缓慢成像的低效显示屏的想法。显示屏为40x25像素网格，每分钟转动10个像素，与现代显示屏形成鲜明对比。

作者最初尝试使用木制材料和不同类型的球体作为像素，包括乒乓球、泡沫球、高尔夫球和Nerf球，但都遇到了成本、重量、易碎性和尺寸不一致等问题。最终，作者在2024年转而采用非球体设计，考虑过翻盖和发光按钮，最后选择了立方体像素。这个项目结合了网络应用、物理控制器、定制CNC构建、3D建模和打印等多项技术，是作者迄今为止最具挑战和野心的项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机械像素显示项目的不同技术实现和改进建议

不同观点：
• fentonc分享了自己制作的类似项目，但采用了打孔卡和手摇的机械方式，所有像素是并行变化的。他对该项目的机制开发感到熟悉，因为两者有很多相似的部分。
• re对项目表示赞赏，并提出了几项改进建议，包括完成提交后将“笔”移开以获得清晰的照片、在网站上显示当前进行中提交的归属信息、以及为已完成提交建立“历史”图库。
• theletterf以幽默的方式提到该项目的刷新率极低，但认为这赋予了“平静技术”新的意义。
• aarondf指出这个项目可能是他见过的每像素成本最高的显示项目，但他对该项目的独特性表示赞赏。
• GistNoesis提出了一种廉价的物理显示实现方法，使用磁性小球和3D打印技术，并讨论了通过电磁头旋转小球的可能性，甚至可以创建一个Ising模型。
• bubblebeard赞赏项目体现了对探索和学习的热爱，认为项目的旅程比目标更重要。
• xpe提出了一种使立方体指向正前方，并通过不同视角同时显示两幅图像的想法。
• TrnsltLife将项目与小说《差分机》中的kinotrope相比较，并分享了一个使用伺服电机实现的kinotrope项目链接。
• mappu提到柏林技术博物馆中有一个类似的全彩显示装置，由12800个立方体组成。
• derefr讨论了一种使用热敏打印机实现的“显示”方案，通过打印新的图像来刷新显示内容。
• saltcured想象了使用木球或彩色球的快速显示方案，并讨论了通过重力或气动驱动扫描线的可能性。
• xpe进一步提出通过某种距离度量来排序图像显示的建议。
• cinntaile提到一个关于对抗图像的鱼项目，并指出通过训练神经网络来解决该问题。
• joemi对项目表示赞赏，并提出了几种加快显示速度的优化建议，包括无需x轴对齐即可旋转整个列或行。
• mister_mort对网站上正在绘制Bad Apple帧的画面表示有趣，并猜测有人会尝试自动提交该视频的帧。

补充讨论：
• 项目引发了关于不同技术实现和改进建议的广泛讨论，包括机械结构、显示速度、成本控制和图像处理等方面。
• 讨论中涉及了多个类似项目的比较，如打孔卡机械显示、伺服电机驱动的kinotrope和柏林技术博物馆的全彩显示。
• 争议焦点在于如何在保持项目独特性的同时，提高显示速度和效率，部分评论者提出了具体的技术方案和优化建议。

44787902.article_content:
I spent 6 years building a ridiculous wooden pixel display
August 2, 2025
TL,DR: I built the world's most impractical 1000-pixel display and anyone in the world can draw on it
If you just want to play with it, goto
kilopx.com
.
The backstory
Six years ago I had an idea to build a large, inefficient display with a web interface that anyone could interact with. I've enjoyed
Danny Rozin's unconvenional mirrors
over the years and was inspired by an
eInk movie player that played at 24 frames per
hour
that got me thinking about a laborious display that could slowly assemble an image.
I landed on the idea of a 40Ã25 pixel grid of pixels, turned one by one by a single mechanism. Compared to our modern displays with millions of pixels changing 60 times a second, a wooden display that changes a single pixel 10 times a
minute
is an incredibly inefficient way to create an image. Conveniently, 40Ã25 = 1,000 pixels, leading to the name
Kilopixel
and the six-letter domain name
kilopx.com
. How do you back down from that? That's the best domain name I've ever owned.
So I got to work. This project has everything: a web app, a physical controller, a custom CNC build, generated gcode, tons of fabrication, 3d modeling, 3d printing, material sourcing - so much to get lost in. It's the most ambitious project I've ever built.
The first prototype: 21Ã3 pixels
My first thought was to use a wooden gantry that would ride on some sort of track. Since I'm most comfortable working with wood, it's my default prototyping medium. However, I quickly pivoted to extruded aluminum and the excellent
hardware kits from Openbuilds
that include pulleys, gantry parts, extruded aluminum, and timing belts. It's very similar to the materials used in 3D printer frames, and connects very easily with off the shelf stepper motors. This allowed me to build a gantry with X and Y, essentially a wall-mounted XY plotter. I built the first prototype with two stepper motors, a Raspberry Pi, a CNC controller, and a beefy power supply. It allowed me to generating and sending instructions to the CNC controller to move to a particular pixel, turning that pixel, and reading values from sensors. It also revealed quite a few problems with my pixel choices and pixel manipulation mechanisms.
1,000 of anything is
expensive
Picking pixels was a real adventure. I've tried ping pong balls, styrofoam balls, bouncy balls, wooden balls, 3d printed balls, golf balls, foam balls...anything approximately spherical and about 1-1.5in in diameter. The problems I encountered were largely cost (even a 50Â¢ ball is $500 of balls), weight (again, a thousand of these things), and availability. For a long time I thought ping pong balls were my best bet, so I purchased a few hundred of them, 3d printed painting jigs, and spray painted them. I used a hot nail to melt two opposite holes on each ball so they could be strung up on the display.
Ping pong balls are basically soda cans
You can stand on a soda can,
as long as it's not open
. Open the can, and it crushes easily. Ping pong balls are the same way. They're relatively strong until you melt two holes in them. Then they can be deformed, which is fatal to any spray paint you've put on them. And not only are they fragile, but the cheap ones are inconsistently sized, and a half millimeter here and there adds up when you have a row of 40 balls. Ping pong balls were a no-go.
Nerfed
My next attempt at a cheap, spherical pixel was foam Nerf balls - much smaller than ping pong balls, and only available in bright colors. They accepted spray paint OK but the paint deteriorated over time.
It was difficult to consistently bore a hole through the nerf balls, and they really liked to grab the wire and were hard to turn. I struggled to consistently turn them and I wasn't thrilled with the bright colors.
I also tried bouncy balls (hard to drill a hole, hard to paint, inconsistent sizes, heavy), wooden balls (not very round, hard to paint a crisp line, heavy), and styrofoam balls (hard to paint with acrylic paint, and they melt with spray paint).
Turning balls
I had the idea to use a small, slow motor to rotate a LEGO wheel against the ping pong ball. I'd use a reflectivity sensor to detect if it was showing black or white, and stop once the pixel was rotated properly. I modeled and printed a custom hub for a LEGO wheel, a few different mechanisms to move the wheel in and out of contact of the sphere, and an interface for the gantry. I tried using a solenoid to push the motor into the ball, which was underpowered, and a servo. Neither approach worked great and ultimately I decided this ball turning approach was a dead end.
Pivoting to non-spherical pixels

and
Chris Morrell on the Over Engineered podcast

44787902.article_summary:
作者花了六年时间打造了一个不切实际的木制像素显示屏，名为"Kilopixel"，包含1000个像素，任何人都可以通过网站kilopx.com进行绘制。这个项目源于作者对Danny Rozin的非传统镜子和一个每小时播放24帧的电子墨水播放器的兴趣，激发了制作一个缓慢成像的低效显示屏的想法。显示屏为40x25像素网格，每分钟转动10个像素，与现代显示屏形成鲜明对比。

作者最初尝试使用木制材料和不同类型的球体作为像素，包括乒乓球、泡沫球、高尔夫球和Nerf球，但都遇到了成本、重量、易碎性和尺寸不一致等问题。最终，作者在2024年转而采用非球体设计，考虑过翻盖和发光按钮，最后选择了立方体像素。这个项目结合了网络应用、物理控制器、定制CNC构建、3D建模和打印等多项技术，是作者迄今为止最具挑战和野心的项目。

data.title: Illinois Bans AI from Providing Therapy
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 伊利诺伊州州长JB普利兹克签署了一项新法律，禁止人工智能（AI）担任治疗师或顾问，仅限于行政或支持角色。该法律规定，只有持牌专业人士才能提供治疗服务，AI不得独立做出治疗决策或生成未经审查的治疗计划。违规者可能面临高达1万美元的罚款。同时，内华达州和犹他州也通过了类似法规，纽约则要求AI在用户表达自杀想法时引导其联系危机热线。这些措施旨在保护患者免受未受监管的AI在医疗保健中的潜在危害。美国心理学会（APA）此前曾与联邦监管机构会面，表达了对AI冒充治疗师的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各评论者对政府是否应监管或禁止AI在医疗领域的应用存在不同看法，并讨论了AI在医疗系统中的潜在影响和问题。

不同观点：
• **SilverElfin** 认为，如果合理应用，AI可以显著提升医疗效果并降低成本，反对以“无意义”的方式禁止AI。他指出，当前的医疗系统存在监管俘获和激励机制失灵的问题，因此过度限制AI可能不利于医疗创新。
  
• **xrd** 支持各州自行监管AI，而不希望AI相关政策通过大型法案（如提到的BBB，即《重建更好法案》）来统一实施。他似乎认为联邦层面的立法可能带来负面影响，而地方政府的独立监管更加灵活和有效。

• **duxup** 分享了对AI在实际应用中可能带来的负面体验的担忧。他提到在YouTube上看到类似AI驱动的治疗广告，感觉这些广告瞄准了脆弱群体，类似于赌博广告的做法，暗示AI可能被滥用于牟利。

补充讨论：
• **SilverElfin** 强调了AI在医疗领域的潜力，但未具体提及如何防止AI滥用或保证其安全性，更多关注的是监管过度的问题。
  
• **xrd** 对大型法案的反对隐含了对联邦政策一刀切的担忧，认为地方政府可能更了解本地需求，但未详细说明各州监管AI的具体利弊。

• **duxup** 提出了AI广告可能带来的伦理问题，特别是针对弱势群体的潜在剥削，指出了AI应用中需要注意的实际风险和滥用问题。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于AI在医疗中的应用应如何被监管，是应由联邦统一立法，还是由各州自主决定。另外，AI的潜在滥用和如何平衡创新与保护消费者利益也是讨论的焦点。

Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed, on Friday, a new measure that bans AI from acting as a therapist or counselor and limits its use to strictly administrative or support roles.
The
Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act
comes as states and federal regulators are starting
to grapple
with how to protect patients from the growing and mostly unregulated use of AI in health care.
The new law prohibits individuals and businesses from advertising or offering any therapy services, including via AI, unless those services are conducted by a licensed professional. It explicitly bans AI from making independent therapeutic decisions, generating treatment plans without the review and approval from a licensed provider, and detecting emotions or mental states.
That said, AI platforms can still be used for administrative tasks, such as managing appointment schedules, processing billing, or taking therapy notes. People or companies that violate the law could face fines of up to $10,000.
âThe people of Illinois deserve quality healthcare from real, qualified professionals and not computer programs that pull information from all corners of the internet to generate responses that harm patients,â said Mario Treto, Jr, secretary of the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation, the agency that is charged with enforcing this new law, in a
press release
.
Meanwhile, other states are also taking action on the issue.
In June,
Nevada banned AI
from providing therapy or behavioral health services that would normally be performed by licensed professionals, particularly in public schools.
Utah passed
several of its own AI regulations
Â earlier this year, including one focusing on mental health chatbots. That law requires companies to clearly disclose that users are interacting with an AI and not a human before a user first uses the chatbot, after seven days of inactivity, and whenever the user asks. The chatbots must also clearly disclose any ads, sponsorships, or paid relationships. Additionally, they’re banned from using user input for targeted ads and are restricted from selling usersâ individually identifiable health information.
And in New York, a new law going into effect on November 5, 2025, will require
AI companions
to direct users who express suicidal thoughts to a mental health crisis hotline.
These new state laws come after the American Psychological Association (APA) met with federal regulators earlier this year to raise concerns that AI posing as therapists could put the public at risk.
In a
blog post
, the APA cited two lawsuits filed by parents whose children used chatbots that allegedly claimed to be licensed therapists. In one case, a boy died by suicide after extensive use of the app. In the other, a child attacked his parents.

data.title: Debian 13 Showing 13% Performance Improvement over Debian 12 on AMD EPYC
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
文章总结如下：

Debian 13预计将于本周末发布，初步测试显示其在AMD EPYC服务器上的性能比Debian 12提升了13%。Debian 13引入了Linux 6.12内核、GNOME 48桌面环境、GCC 14.2编译器等更新，并正式支持RISC-V 64位、HTTP启动以及完成64位"time_t" ABI过渡。作者通过130项基准测试对比Debian 12和Debian 13，结果显示Debian 13在现代硬件上表现更佳，尤其是在代码编译、数据库性能和AI基准测试方面有显著提升。此外，Debian 13还包括许多软件包的升级和其他技术改进。

Debian 13 Showing 13% Performance Improvement Over Debian 12 On AMD EPYC
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Operating Systems
on 5 August 2025 at 12:00 PM EDT.
Page 1 of 6
.
7 Comments
.
If all goes according to plan
Debian 13.0 will be released this weekend
. Already in its effectively final state aside from any last minute fixes, I've begun running Debian 13 testing builds on various systems in the lab to great success. With two years since Debian 12, the new software packages of Debian 13 help in delivering better performance especially on modern systems. Here is a look at Debian 12 versus Debian 13 performance on an AMD EPYC server across 130 benchmarks. Coincidentally, Debian 13 is coming in at 13% faster than Debian 12.
Debian 13
is shaping up to be another strong release for this Linux distribution. Going from Debian 12 to Debian 13 means jumping from Linux 6.1 to Linux 6.12 LTS, GNOME 43 to GNOME 48 for the default desktop, GCC 12.2 to the GCC 14.2 compiler used by default, and a wealth of other package upgrades like Python 3.11 to Python 3.13 and OpenJDK Java 21 replacing Java 17 as the default.
There are tons of other software updates too throughout the Debian repository with this imminent Debian 13 "Trixie" release. Aside from the package upgrades, Debian 13 is introducing official support for RISC-V 64-bit, HTTP boot support using UEFI and U-Boot, completing the 64-bit "time_t" ABI transition, continued work on reproducible builds, and countless other refinements made over the past two years.
For getting an idea of the Debian 13 performance on modern hardware, I ran 130 benchmarks across a clean install of Debian 12.11 followed by a clean install of Debian 13.0 testing as of last week. The same server was used for all of the testing with being a high-end AMD EPYC 9965 2P server with 1.5TB of RAM and 1TB NVMe SSD.

data.title: Poor sleep linked to 172 diseases, including dementia, Parkinson's, diabetes
data.author: brandonb
data.article_summary: 一项新研究发现，不良睡眠模式与172种疾病相关，包括痴呆、糖尿病和帕金森病等。研究分析了英国生物银行中超过88,000名成人的医疗数据，发现其中92种疾病的风险有超过20%与不良睡眠行为相关。这些疾病包括年龄相关的身体虚弱、坏疽、纤维化和肝硬化等，其中42种疾病的风险至少增加了一倍。研究强调，睡眠规律性比睡眠时长更重要，睡眠节奏紊乱可能诱发多种疾病。尽管研究显示了关联性，但尚未确定因果关系。未来研究将关注如何通过改善睡眠来预防或治疗这些疾病。

Share on Pinterest
Researchers have found a link between sleep quality and disease risk with many chronic conditions. Catherine Falls Commercial/Getty Images
Getting enough quality sleep every night is important for good health, but the extent it affects overall health is still being researched.
A new study has linked 172 different diseases, including dementia, diabetes, and Parkinson’s disease to poor sleep patterns.
Of those diseases, 92 of them had over 20% of their risk correlated with poor sleep behavior.
Getting
enough quality sleep
every night is important for
good health
. However, some people may still be unclear about what “quality sleep” entails and what impact sleep really has on their health.
“[Until] now we have not completely understood how sleep builds our health,”
Qing Chen
, PhD, associate professor at the Institute of Toxicology in the College of Preventive Medicine at the Third Military Medical University (Army Medical University) in China, told
Medical News Today
.
“Maybe we only know that sleep deprivation is harmful. No scientist has 100% confidence to tell us when we should sleep or when we should not sleep, [or] whether there are additional sleep tips that are important for health,“ said Chen. “This is not enough to make a really healthy sleep schedule.”
Chen is the co-lead author of a study recently published in the journal
Health Data Science
that has linked 172 different diseases to poor sleep patterns. Of those diseases, 92 had over 20% of the risk correlated with poor sleep behavior.
More than 20% of risk for 92 diseases linked to poor sleep
For this study, researchers analyzed medical data from more than 88,000 adults in the
UK Biobank
database to measure both their sleep traits and disease diagnoses.
After an average 7-year follow-up, researchers associated 172 diseases with poor sleep patterns, including irregular bedtimes and off-
circadian rhythms
.
Of these, the risk for 42 diseases was at least doubled, including age-related physical debility,
gangrene
,
fibrosis
, and
cirrhosis
of the liver.
Chen and his team also discovered that 92 of the 172 diseases had more than 20% of their risk traceable to poor sleep, including dementia, primary hypertension,
Parkinson’s disease
,
type 2 diabetes
, and
acute kidney failure
.
“Sleep regularity (rhythm) should be taken into consideration, or a number of diseases may be induced, even if sleep duration is adequate,” Chen said. “This is because sleep rhythm and sleep duration may be in charge of different aspects of our health.”
“
We want to understand why disruption of sleep rhythm induces diseases, and how can we prevent or cure the diseases induced by sleep rhythm disruption,” he commented, when asked about the next steps for this research.
Does lack of sleep cause these diseases?
MNT
spoke with
Matthew Scharf
, MD, PhD, regional sleep medicine director at Hackensack Meridian Health, and associate professor at Hackensack Meridian Medical School in New Jersey, about this study.
Scharf, who was not involved in the research, commented that this study builds on mounting evidence showing that insufficient or poor sleep can negatively impact health.
“Strengths of the study include use of objective data and a very large sample size,” he explained. “However, it shows many associations but does not necessarily show causation.”
“Sleep has emerged as an important modifiable behavior to improve health and longevity,” Scharf continued. “The goal is to find out how sleep is linked with various diseases in order to have targeted interventions. For example, some groups may benefit from having a longer sleep duration. Others may benefit from having a more regular sleep schedule.”
For next steps in this research, Scharf said the key piece would be to see if targeted interventions improve outcomes in each patient population.
“For example, in patients with Parkinson’s disease, would a program that promoted a regular bedtime routine improve Parkinson’s disease-related symptoms or quality of life metrics?” he asked.
Sleep regularity matters more than sleep duration
Daniel Truong
, MD, a neurologist and medical director of the Truong Neuroscience Institute at MemorialCare Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA and editor in chief of the Journal of Clinical Parkinsonism and Related Disorders
,
who was not involved in the recent study, told
MNT
that his reaction to this study’s findings was one of surprising clarity: Sleep regularity matters more than sleep duration in explaining disease risk.

data.title: Show HN: Scar – A programming language for easy concurrency and parallelism
data.author: death_eternal
data.article_summary: Scar是一种现代系统编程语言，旨在简化并发处理，同时保持高效能和性能。它具备内置的并发管理功能，通过`parallel`块自然表达并行操作，并自动处理线程管理。Scar语法简洁、可读性高，专注于解决问题而非应对语言复杂性。它内置内存安全功能，防止常见错误，同时保持系统级性能。通过零成本抽象和与C语言的无缝互操作，Scar能够编译成高效的本地代码。此外，Scar支持智能类型推断，减少样板代码，并提供IDE支持。示例包括并行处理数据和定义简洁的类结构。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新编程语言的设计及其对并发和并行的支持

不同观点：
• **death_eternal** 认为Nim语言在多线程和数值计算方面存在不足，因此开始开发一种新语言。该语言通过内置的并发支持（如parallel blocks和parallel fors）来自动处理线程同步问题，且拥有可选的GC和C后端。目前该语言仍在开发中，但已有一些基本示例。
• **ljchen** 对新语言的并发特性表示兴趣，但质疑其使用场景，认为关注并发和并行的开发者通常也关注性能，因此想知道新语言在性能方面的优势和具体使用场景。
• **renox** 对新语言使用C风格的"%d"格式化字符串提出批评，认为Python的格式化字符串方式更为先进。

补充讨论：
• **death_eternal** 提供了新语言的具体例子，展示了如何使用parallel blocks和parallel fors来简化并发代码的编写。
• **ljchen** 的质疑引出了对新语言性能和实际应用场景的讨论，这可能是新语言需要进一步澄清和证明的关键点。
• **renox** 对语法细节提出了改进建议，强调了新语言在设计时应考虑更现代的语法特性。

争议焦点：
• 新语言在并发和并行处理方面的实际性能和使用场景。
• 新语言在格式化字符串等语法设计上的选择。

data.title: Call to a local Social Security may be picked up by someone who can't help
data.author: duxup
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了美国社会保障局（Social Security Administration, SSA）为减少电话服务等待时间而实施的新“电话共享”系统。该系统将本地办公室的来电转接到其他地区办公室，但接听人员可能无法处理来电者的问题，因为这些问题仅限于特定管辖范围。这一变化旨在提高服务效率，但实际上可能导致问题解决的延迟，尤其是对没有代理人帮助的来电者。一些员工和维权人士担心，这不仅浪费时间，还可能削弱公众对系统的信任。此外，员工对该系统的实施时间及细节缺乏明确信息，感到困惑和压力。文章指出，该系统的实施缺乏充分的沟通和准备，可能导致更多问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对呼叫中心管理方式的评价及对相关问题是否值得关注的看法

不同观点：
• **duxup 的观点**：呼叫中心的新管理层为了显示成绩，常常通过随意分配电话来降低等待时间，而不考虑这种方式是否对长期运营有益。这种做法被认为是表面功夫，实际上并不能解决问题。例子包括新管理层仅关注降低等待时间，而不关心通话质量或问题解决率。

• **dmitrygr 的观点**：认为呼叫中心效率低下的问题已经是众所周知的常态，没有什么值得特别关注的。虽然这些问题确实存在且不好，但并不新鲜，因此不值得作为新闻报道。dmitrygr 对其他人对此问题表现出的惊讶或关注表示不理解。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于，duxup 认为随意分配电话以降低等待时间是一种短视的管理策略，而 dmitrygr 则认为这种低效现象早已普遍存在，不值得特别关注或报道。
• duxup 强调了管理层为了短期成绩而忽视长期效益的问题，而 dmitrygr 则关注这种现象的普遍性和是否值得媒体关注。
• 例子方面，duxup 基于自身在大学期间于呼叫中心工作的经验，提供了具体管理实践的描述，而 dmitrygr 则以反问的方式质疑该问题的新闻价值。

Why Social Security's new ‘phone sharing’ system may slow help
Phone calls to local Social Security offices are currently being rerouted to other field offices — often to staff who don't have jurisdiction over the caller's case, employees say.
Politics
Your call to a local Social Security office may be picked up by someone who can't help
August 5, 2025
11:28 AM ET
Ashley Lopez
A Social Security Administration office building is seen on March 6 in Nashville, Tenn.
George Walker IV/AP
hide caption
toggle caption
George Walker IV/AP
Phone calls to local Social Security offices are currently being rerouted to other field offices — often to staff who don't have jurisdiction over the caller's case, employees say.
Disability advocates and experts warn this is making it harder for people to get help.
The latest change is part of the Social Security Administration's
ongoing efforts
to bring down wait times for phone services.
In a statement to NPR, a spokesperson for the agency said that "the goal of the phone sharing system is to enhance customer service by reducing wait times and addressing customer needs at the first point of contact.
Sponsor Message
"Under the newly implemented system, calls to local field offices may be routed to available staff at other field offices, regardless of geographic location, to help manage high call volumes."
Politics
Efforts to shrink Social Security's phone wait times are putting a strain elsewhere
But Angela Digeronimo, a claims specialist in Woodbridge, N.J., and president of a union that represents employees at 25 offices in the state, told NPR this new system creates a "hit or miss" situation for people calling in to their local office.
Digeronimo said the intention of this change "may have been to not have callers waiting," which is a good thing. But in practice, she said, it delays getting an issue sorted if a caller is rerouted to a local office that can't actually fix their problem.
"If it's someone else's office, the jurisdiction is someone else's," she said. "You can't take action on it because your office does not have the ability to clear that claim. You have to refer it over to the servicing office, which is what the member of the public thought they were doing. So, it gets a little bit cumbersome."
A spokesperson for the agency rebutted the claim that callers are getting routed to offices that can't help.
"All SSA field offices are equipped to handle inquiries and resolve issues for callers, irrespective of where a caller lives or where their case originated," the spokesperson said in a statement. "SSA staff across the country have access to the necessary systems and information to assist with a wide range of Social Security matters."
Sponsor Message
But Amber Westbrook, a local union chapter president and field office employee in the Chicago region, said that's just not how the system works.
"Our system is very specific to the office that we can do things in," she explained. "So I, physically, if another claim is open in another office, I cannot clear their case. It's just kind of the way that they retain that to make sure that things are accurate and complete."
Westbrook said workers in other field offices may be able to see what's going on with someone's case, but if they're in the wrong jurisdiction they can't "actually take care of the issue."
Business
What Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act means for taxes on Social Security
Jen Burdick, a supervising attorney at Community Legal Services of Philadelphia, said the new phone sharing system is creating a situation where it is taking her group "more time to help people" get and keep Social Security disability benefits.
"I feel like perhaps there was good intentions here, but this is ineffective and this is going to waste more people's time, at least when I am rerouted to another office," she said.
Burdick said she is most concerned, though, about individuals who don't have a representative helping them.
"How does that impact them? Does that make them think that they can't call SSA in the future?" she asked. "I'm worried that it'll undermine confidence in the system."
For employees, Westbrook said there's also been very little communicated about how long this program will be in place.
"They haven't really given us a whole lot of idea of how long this is going to last," she said. "Things [are] changing so rapidly within the agency … something may be different tomorrow than it is today. It's been a whirlwind for people."
Nancy Altman — president of Social Security Works, a group that advocates for the expansion of Social Security — said in past administrations officials would have gotten input from every level before implementing a new system.

44800267.article_content:
Cognition, the AI coding startup that acquired rival company Windsurf three weeks ago, laid off 30 employees last week and is offering buyouts to the roughly 200 remaining employees on the team,
reports The Information
.
This is the latest bout of whiplash that Windsurf employees have faced after a tumultuous stretch for the company. The startup was initially almost acquired by OpenAI, then lost its
CEO, co-founder, and research leads to Google
in a $2.4 billion deal known as a reverse-acquihire (where Google hired the key talent rather than buying the company), before ultimately getting
acquired by Cognition
.
At the time of the acquisition, Cognition stated that 100% of Windsurf employees would receive financial compensation as part of the deal and
stressed
that the company was excited to bring on Windsurf’s “world-class people” to develop top-notch coding tools.
Now, it’s becoming clear that Windsurf’s intellectual property, not its talent, was the real buy.
According to an email The Information viewed, employees were given until August 10 to decide whether they want to take the buyout, which amounts to nine months of salary. Those who choose to stay are reportedly required to spend six days at the office and clock more than 80-hour weeks — draconian conditions that have become
table stakes among workers at top AI firms.
“We don’t believe in work-life balance—building the future of software engineering is a mission we all care so deeply about that we couldn’t possibly separate the two,” wrote Cognition CEO Scott Wu in the email.
TechCrunch has reached out to Cognition for more details.

data.title: DeepMind reveals Genie 3 "world model" creates real-time interactive simulations
data.author: DocFeind
data.article_summary: Google DeepMind推出Genie 3，这是一款能够通过提示或图像生成互动世界的先进模型。与前代Genie 2相比，Genie 3具有更高的视觉保真度，并能实时运行，支持720p分辨率和24帧每秒的导航。它还能记住生成的世界，保持视觉元素的一致性，克服了Genie 2记忆时间短的局限。不过，Genie 3仍有不足，如无法模拟真实世界位置，且生成的细节只能保持数分钟。此外，AI代理在世界模型中的互动有限，缺乏高层次的推理能力。尽管如此，Genie 3在合成数据和人工智能研究方面具有重要潜力，可能推动人工通用智能（AGI）的发展。目前，该工具主要用于研究，而非商业应用。
